lsj_entry_text: ἔνιοι, αι, α, some; never in Ep. , Lyr., or Att. Poets before Men. , exc. Ar. Pl. 867 (cf. however ἐνίοτε); first used in Ion. Prose, as Hdt. 1.120 , 8.56 , Hp. Praec. 6 ; πολλοὶ μὲν . . ἔνιοι δὲ . . Lys. 25.19 ; ἔνιοι μὲν . . ἔνιοι δὲ . . Pl. Tht. 151a , X. Mem. 4.2.38 ; ἔνιοι μὲν . . οἱ δὲ . . Pl. Mx. 238e ; ἔνιοί τινες Isoc. 15.258 : later in sg., οὐ πᾶσα κίνησις θερμαίνει, ἀλλ' ἐνία ψύχει Arist. Pr. 884b13 , cf. Thphr. Vert. 1 ; περὶ ψυχῆς ἐνίας θεωρῆσαι Arist. greek_sentence: Τοῖς μὲν παλαιοῖς ἰατροῖς ἀπόχρη μόνον τοῦτο εἰποῦσιν, ὡς κατὰ περίοδον ἐνίοις τῶν νοσημάτων οἱ παροξυσμοὶ γίνονται, μηκέτι προστιθεμένοις, τί σημαίνει τοὔνομα ἡ περίοδος.
english_sentence_A: For the ancient physicians it was enough to say only this, that in some of the diseases the paroxysms occur according to a period, without adding further what the name "period" signifies.
english_sentence_B: For the ancient physicians it was enough to say only this, that in some of the diseases the paroxysms occur according to a period, without going on to add what the name 'period' signifies.

lsj_entry_text: τύπ-ος [υ], ὁ, (τύπτω) blow, τ. ἀντίτυπος Orac. ap. Hdt. 1.67 ; beat of horses' hoofs, v.l. for κτὺπος in X. Eq. 11.12 ; αἰθερίου πατάγοιο τ. βρονταῖον ἀκούων Nonn. D. 20.351 ; so perh. νάβλα τ. Sopat. 16 . the effect of a blow or of pressure: impression of a seal, τύποι σφενδόνης χρυσηλάτου E. Hipp. 862 , cf. Pl. Tht. 192a , 194b , Chrysipp.Stoic. 2.23 , Luc. Alex. 21 ; τ. ἐνσημήνασθαί τινι Pl. R. 377b ; stamp on a coin, τὰ ἀκριβῆ τὸν τ. Luc. Hist.Conscr. 10 , cf. Hero *Mens. 60 , Hsch. s.v. Κυζικηνοι στατῆρες; on a branding-iron, ὄ τ. τοῦ καυτῆρος ἔστω ἀλώπηξ ἢ πίθηκος Luc. Pisc. 46 : generally, print, impression, χύτρας τύπον ἀρθείσης ἐν σποδῷ μὴ ἀπολιπεῖν, ἀλλὰ συγχεῖν Plu. 2.727c , cf. 982b , Iamb. Protr. 21 . κθ', Gp. 2.20.1 ; στίβου γ' οὐδεὶς τ. no footprint, S. Ph. 29 ( v.l. κτύπος ); ὡς ἡδὺς ἐν πόρπακι σὸς (sc. τοῦ βραχίονος) κεῖται τύπος thy imprint, (O arm), E. Tr. 1196 (σῷ cj. Dobree); τ. ὀδόντων imprint of teeth, AP 6.57.5 (Paul. Sil.); print, βάλω τὸν δάκτυλόν μου εἰς τὸν τ. τῶν ἥλων Ev.Jo. 20.25 ; οἱ τ. τῶν πληγῶν Ath. 13.585c . impressions supposed by Democr. and Epicur. to be made on the air by things seen, and to travel through space, Thphr. Sens. 52 , Epicur. Ep. 1p.9U. , Nat. 2.6 , al.; ὁ θεὸς . . πνεῦμα ἐνεκέρασεν [τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖσ] οὕτως ἰσχυρὸν καὶ φιλότεχνον ὥστε ἀναμάσσεσθαι τοὺς τ. τῶν ὁρωμένων Arr. Epict. 2.23.3 . hollow mould or matrix, καθάπερ ἐν τύπῳ τὰ σχήματα πλασθῆναι Arist. PA 676b9 , cf. Pr. 892b2 ; used by κοροπλάθοι, D.Chr. 60.9 , Procl. in Ti. 1.335 , 394 D. , cf. Hsch. s.v. χοάνη ; by fruit-growers, to shape the fruit while growing, Gp. 10.9.3 ; die used in striking coins, metaph., Κύπριος χαρακτήρ τ' ἐν γυναικείοις τύποις εἰκὼς πέπληκται τεκτόνων πρὸς ἀρσένων A. Supp. 282 . engraved mark, engraving, δέλτον χαλκῆν τύπους ἔχουσαν ἀρχαίων γραμμάτων engravings of letters, i. e. engraved letters, Plu. Alex. 17 , cf. Pl. Phdr. 275a ; τὰ γεγραμμένα τύποις Id. Ep. 343a ; τὸ μέτρον τοῦ ποδὸς ὑποτέτακται τούτοις τοῖς τ. the length of the foot is subjoined in this engraving, Rev.Bibl. 35.285 (Jerusalem). the depression between the underlip and chin, Poll. 2.90 . pip on dice, Id. 9.95 . cast or replica made in a mould, τ. κατάμακτος IG 22.1534.87 ; τ. ἔγμακτος ib. 64 . figure worked in relief, whether made by moulding, modelling, or sculpture, αἱμασιὴ ἐγγεγλυμμένη τύποισι Hdt. 2.138 , cf. 106 , 136 , 148 , 153 ; θεοῦ τ. μὴ ἐπίγλυφε δακτυλίῳ Iamb. Protr. 21 .κγ ́; σιδηρονώτοις ἀσπίδος τύποις E. Ph. 1130 ; χρυσοκόλλητοι τ. Id. Rh. 305 ; τ. ἀργυροῦς IG 22.1533.30 , 11(2).161 B 77 , cf. 115 (Delos, iii B. C.); τύπους ἐργάσασθαι καὶ παρέχειν ib. 42(1).102.36 (Epid., iv B. C.); tablet bearing a relief, καθελέσθαι τοὺς τ. καὶ εἴ τι ἄλλο ἐστὶν ἀργυροῦν ἢ χρυσοῦν ib. 22.839.30 , cf. 56 , al.; τ. Synt. 278.25 . archetype, pattern, model, capable of exact repetition in numerous instances, αὑτὸν ἐκμάττειν . . εἰς τοὺς τῶν κακιόνων τ. Pl. R. 396e ; οἰκισταῖς (sc. πόλεως) τοὺς μὲν τ. προσήκει εἰδέναι, ἐν οἷς δεῖ μυθολογεῖν τοὺς ποιητάς . . , οὐ μὴν αὐτοῖς γε ποιητέον μύθους· . . οἱ τ. περὶ θεολογίας τίνες ἂν εἶεν; ib. 379a , cf. 380c . character recognizable in a number of instances, general character, type, πάντα ὅσα τοῦ τ. τούτου Id. greek_sentence: ὅσοι μὲν οὖν ἄχρι τῆς περὶ τοὺς ὅρους φιλοτιμίας προεληλύθασι συγχωροῦντες ἐκ τῶν τριῶν ὀνομάτων ἕν τι σημαίνεσθαι, τύπου καὶ περιόδου καὶ τάξεως, ἐλάττονα φλυαροῦσιν· ὅσοι δὲ περίοδον μὲν ὀνομάζουσι τὸν χρόνον, δι’ ὅν τι ταὐτὸν γίγνεται, τύπον δὲ οὐχ ἁπλῶς ἅπαντα τὸν τοιοῦτον χρόνον, ἀλλ’ ὅταν ὁλοκλήροις ἡμέραις τε καὶ νυξὶ περιγράφηται, μακρὰς οὗτοι καὶ ἀχρήστους φλυαρίας καταβάλλονται, καὶ διὰ τοῦθ’ αὑτῶν τε καὶ τῶν μαθητῶν κατατρίψαντες τὸν χρόνον, ὅταν ἐπὶ τοὺς κάμνοντας ἀφίκωνται, χείρους εἰσὶν ἰδιώτου παντός.
english_sentence_A: Now those who have advanced only as far as the rivalry over definitions, while conceding that one single thing is signified by the three names—type, period, and order—talk less nonsense; but those who call 'period' the time in the course of which some identical thing occurs, and 'type' not simply every such time, but only when it is circumscribed by whole days and nights—these lay down long and useless nonsense, and, having on this account wasted both their own time and that of their pupils, when they come to the sick they are worse than any layman.
english_sentence_B: Now those who have advanced only as far as contentious zeal about definitions, while conceding that one single thing is signified by the three names, 'type', 'period' and 'order', talk less nonsense. But those who call 'period' the time at the interval of which the same thing occurs, and 'type' not simply every such time but only when it is bounded by whole days and nights, these men put forth long and useless nonsense; and having on this account wasted both their own time and that of their pupils, when they come to the sick they are worse than any layman.

english_sentence_A: For a layman possessed of sense, when he sees someone suffering a paroxysm every day, whether the paroxysm comes a little late or anticipates, has some impression of the period called [477] quotidian; and if someone should be both industrious and fond of medicine, some notion enters him of two tertians or three quartans, and he asks that this be determined by the physicians.
english_sentence_B: For a layman of sense, when he sees someone suffering a paroxysm each day, whether the paroxysm is slightly delayed or comes early, forms some impression of the period called [477] quotidian; and if he should also be diligent and fond of medicine, some notion enters his mind of two tertians or three quartans, and he thinks it right that this be determined by the physicians.

greek_sentence: οἱ δὲ ταῖς εἰρημέναις ὑποθέσεσι δουλεύοντες, ἐὰν ἐντύχωσιν ἀῤῥώστῳ δυοῖν ὥραιν ἑκάστης ἡμέρας τὸν παροξυσμὸν ἔχοντι προληπτικὸν, εἴκοσι μὲν εἶναι καὶ δυοῖν ὥραιν φασὶ τὴν περίοδον, τὸν δ’ ὅλον τύπον οὐχ ἁπλοῦν, ἀλλά τινα σύνθετον ὑπάρχειν νομίζουσιν· εἶτα ζητήσαντες ἱκανῶς καὶ λογισάμενοι κατὰ σφᾶς αὑτοὺς, οἱ μὲν ἐπὶ δακτύλων, οἱ δὲ καὶ ἐπὶ διαγράμματος ἔν τινι βιβλίῳ γεγραμμένου, δώδεκά φασιν εἶναι δωδεκαταίους τὸν τοιοῦτον τύπον.
english_sentence_A: But those who are enslaved to the aforesaid hypotheses, if they encounter a sick person who has his paroxysm anticipating by two hours each day, say that the period is one of twenty-two hours, and they consider the whole type to be not simple but some composite one; then, having investigated sufficiently and reckoned it up by themselves, some on their fingers, others even on a diagram drawn in some book, they say that such a type is twelve twelfth-day fevers.
english_sentence_B: But those who are enslaved to the hypotheses just mentioned, if they come upon a patient who has the paroxysm coming two hours early each day, say that the period is of twenty-two hours, and they consider that the whole type is not simple but a compound one. Then, after inquiring at length and reckoning among themselves, some on their fingers, others on a diagram drawn in some book, they declare such a type to be twelve twelfth-day fevers.

lsj_entry_text: ὥρα (C), Ion. ὥρη, ἡ: Ep. gen. pl. ὡράων, Ion. ὡρέων: loc. pl. ὥρασι, q. v. any period, fixed by natural laws and revolutions, whether of the year, month, or day (the sense 'day' is implied in the compd. ἑπτάωρος, q. v.), νυκτός τε ὥραν καὶ μηνὸς καὶ ἐνιαυτοῦ X. Mem. 4.7.4 , cf. E. Alc. 449 (lyr.), Pl. R. 527d ; τοῦ γνώμονος ἡ σκιὰ ἐπιοῦσα ἐπὶ τὰς γραμμὰς σημαίνει τὰς ὥρας τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ καὶ τῆς ἡμέρας IG 12(8).240 (Samothrace): but specially, in Hom. , part of the year, season; mostly in pl., the seasons, ὅτε τέτρατον ἦλθεν ἔτος καὶ ἐπήλυθον ὧραι Od. 2.107 , 19.152 ; ἀλλ' ὅτε δὴ μῆνές τε καὶ ἡμέραι ἐξετελεῦντο, ἂψ περιτελλομένου ἔτεος, καὶ ἐπήλυθον ὧραι 11.295 , 14.294 ; ἀλλ' ὅτε δή ῥ' ἐνιαυτὸς ἔην, περὶ δ' ἔτραπον ὧραι 10.469 , cf. Hes. Th. 58 ; Διὸς ὧραι Od. 24.344 , cf. Pi. O. 4.2 ; ὁ κύκλος τῶν ὡρέων ἐς τὠυτὸ περιιών Hdt. 2.4 , cf. 1.32 ; δυώδεκα μέρεα δασαμένους τῶν ὡρέων ἐς [τὸν ἐνιαυτόν] Id. 2.4 ; οὐ μεταλλάσσουσι αἱ ὧραι ib. 77 ; περιτελλομέναις ὥραις S. OT 156 (lyr.); πάσαις ὥραις at all seasons, Id. Fr. 592.6 (lyr.), Ar. Av. 696 (anap.); ὧραι ἐτῶν καὶ ἐνιαυτῶν Pl. Lg. 906c , cf. Smp. 188a , etc.; τῆς . . ὥρας τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ταύτης οὔσης, ἐν ᾗ ἀσθενοῦσιν ἄνθρωποι μάλιστα Th. 7.47 ; χαλεπὴ ὥ. a bad season, Pl. Prt. 344d ; ἀ δ' ὤρα χαλέπα Alc. 39 ; ἡ ὥ. αὕτη this season, X. Cyn. 7.1 , cf. 5.6 ; κατὰ τὰς ὥρας according to the seasons, Arist. GA 786a31 ; οἱ περὶ τὴν ὥραν χρόνοι Id. Pol. 1335a37 .— Hom. and Hes. distinguish three seasons, and express each by the sg. ὥρη, with a word added to specify each: spring, ἔαρος . . ὥρη Il. 6.148 ; ὥρη εἰαρινή 2.471 , 16.643 , Od. 18.367 , etc.; so in Trag. and Att. , ἦρος ὥρα or ὧραι, Ar. Nu. 1008 (anap.), E. Cyc. 508 (lyr.); ὥρα νέα Ar. Eq. 419 ; νεᾶνις E. Ph. 786 (lyr.); v. infr. 2 . summer, θέρεος ὥρη Hes. Op. 584 , 664 ; ὥρα θερινή X. Cyn. 9.20 , Pl. greek_sentence: οἱ δὲ ταῖς εἰρημέναις ὑποθέσεσι δουλεύοντες, ἐὰν ἐντύχωσιν ἀῤῥώστῳ δυοῖν ὥραιν ἑκάστης ἡμέρας τὸν παροξυσμὸν ἔχοντι προληπτικὸν, εἴκοσι μὲν εἶναι καὶ δυοῖν ὥραιν φασὶ τὴν περίοδον, τὸν δ’ ὅλον τύπον οὐχ ἁπλοῦν, ἀλλά τινα σύνθετον ὑπάρχειν νομίζουσιν· εἶτα ζητήσαντες ἱκανῶς καὶ λογισάμενοι κατὰ σφᾶς αὑτοὺς, οἱ μὲν ἐπὶ δακτύλων, οἱ δὲ καὶ ἐπὶ διαγράμματος ἔν τινι βιβλίῳ γεγραμμένου, δώδεκά φασιν εἶναι δωδεκαταίους τὸν τοιοῦτον τύπον.
english_sentence_A: But those who are enslaved to the aforesaid hypotheses, if they encounter a sick person who has his paroxysm anticipating by two hours each day, say that the period is one of twenty-two hours, and they consider the whole type to be not simple but some composite one; then, having investigated sufficiently and reckoned it up by themselves, some on their fingers, others even on a diagram drawn in some book, they say that such a type is twelve twelfth-day fevers.
english_sentence_B: But those who are enslaved to the hypotheses just mentioned, if they come upon a patient who has the paroxysm coming two hours early each day, say that the period is of twenty-two hours, and they consider that the whole type is not simple but a compound one. Then, after inquiring at length and reckoning among themselves, some on their fingers, others on a diagram drawn in some book, they declare such a type to be twelve twelfth-day fevers.

greek_sentence: ἔτι δὲ μᾶλλον ὅταν ὥρᾳ μιᾷ ποτε θεάσωνται τὸν παροξυσμὸν προλαμβάνοντα, καὶ τότε ἀποφαίνονται δ΄ εἶναι καὶ κ΄ εἰκοστοτεταρταίους, αὐτοί τε καταγελῶνται καί τινα τοῖς ἄλλοις ἰατροῖς ὑποψίαν ἀγνοίας παρὰ τοῖς ἰδιώταις παρασκευάζουσιν.
english_sentence_A: And still more, when at some time they see the paroxysm anticipating by one hour, and then declare that there are twenty-four twenty-fourth-day fevers, they are both laughed at themselves and create among laymen some suspicion of ignorance against the other physicians.
english_sentence_B: Still more is this so whenever they at some time see the paroxysm coming one hour early, and then declare it to be 24 twenty-fourth-day fevers: they are themselves laughed at, and they create among laymen a certain suspicion of ignorance against the other physicians too.

english_sentence_A: For when they see those men discovering from a book, with a certain solemnity, as though it were some matter of the greatest importance, twenty-four twenty-fourth-day fevers, [478] it comes over them to condemn all those who read books, and they entrust themselves rather to those who handle the art by irrational routine.

greek_sentence: ἐὰν γοῦν τις ἕπηται ταῖς ὑποθέσεσι τῶν τὰ τοιαῦτα ληρούντων ἰατρῶν, καὶ τὸν τριταῖον, ὅταν ἤτοι προλαμβάνῃ μίαν ὥραν ἢ ὑστερίζη, πάντα μᾶλλον ἢ τριταῖον ἐρεῖ.
english_sentence_A: At any rate, if anyone follows the hypotheses of the physicians who talk such nonsense, he will call even the tertian, whenever it either anticipates by one hour or lags behind, anything rather than a tertian.
english_sentence_B: At any rate, if one follows the hypotheses of the physicians who talk such nonsense, he will call even the tertian, whenever it either anticipates by one hour or is delayed, anything rather than a tertian.

english_sentence_A: "But you," I said, "describe a paroxysm belonging to a most mild disease, and then by the continuity of the periods you declare it in turn most deadly." "Do not consider at all for the present," he said, "whether the hypothesis is impossible or possible, but allow such things to be investigated for the sake of exercise.

english_sentence_A: "But you," I said, "describe a paroxysm belonging to a most mild disease, and then by the continuity of the periods you declare it in turn most deadly." english_sentence_B: 'You,' I said, 'describe a paroxysm of a disease that is most mild, but by the continuity of its periods you then show the same disease to be most deadly.' 'For the present at least,' he said, 'do not consider at all whether the hypothesis is impossible or possible, but allow such questions to be investigated for the sake of exercise.

english_sentence_A: One must therefore try right from the beginning to diagnose what sort of fever it is, as has been shown in the commentaries On Crises, and for the most part it is possible to know this securely through the signs set out in those; but if some ambiguity should arise on the first day, it must be decided on the second; and if it should ever escape this day too, it will in any case be recognized on the third; and if indeed it should ever escape this too, as happens rarely, still on the fourth it will of necessity be recognized; but if even on this day someone has not yet recognized the form of the disease, but is still at a loss, this man is ignorant of a large part of the art.

greek_sentence: τά τε γὰρ ἄλλα καὶ οἱ παροξυσμοὶ πάντες οἱ ἐν τοῖς πυρετοῖς ἤτοι καθ’ ἑκάστην ἡμέραν, ἢ διὰ τρίτης, ἢ διὰ τετάρτης ἀπαντῶσιν· ἐν μὲν τοῖς πλείστοις νοσήμασιν, ἐφ’ ὧν δὴ καὶ μάλιστά ἐστι χρεία τῆς [481] προγνώσεως τοῦ μέλλοντος ἔσεσθαι παροξυσμοῦ, διὰ τρίτης καὶ καθ’ ἑκάστην ἡμέραν· ἐν ὀλιγίστοις δέ τισι διὰ τετάρτης.
english_sentence_A: For, apart from everything else, all the paroxysms in fevers occur either every day, or every third day, or every fourth day: in most diseases—those in which indeed there is the greatest need of [481] the prognosis of the paroxysm that is going to occur—every third day and every day; in a very few, every fourth day.
english_sentence_B: For, among other things, all the paroxysms in fevers occur either every day, or every third day, or every fourth day: in the majority of diseases, in which there is indeed the greatest need for [481] foreknowledge of the paroxysm that is going to occur, every third day and every day; in a very few, every fourth day.

english_sentence_A: But perhaps one of these more recent sophists says that certain periods also occur every fifth day, and every sixth and seventh, and certain others extending over very many days—men whom one may truly count blessed for their marvellous intelligence, if they do not follow what results from their own statements, utterly destroying the usefulness of the whole treatise on types.
english_sentence_B: But perhaps one of these more recent sophists says that some periods also occur every fifth day, and every sixth and seventh, and certain others extending to a great many days. One may truly felicitate such people on their wonderful intelligence, if they do not perceive that by what they say they utterly abolish the usefulness of the whole treatise on types.

greek_sentence: ἐνδέχεται μὲν οὖν καὶ τοιαύτην εἶναι τὴν ἐπιπλοκὴν τῶν ἁπλῶν περιόδων, ὡς ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ τῶν ἡμερῶν ἀμφημερινὸν ἦρχθαι· κατὰ δὲ τὴν δευτέραν τριταῖον· ἐν δὲ τῇ τρίτῃ δύνασθαι μὲν καὶ τριταῖον, δύνασθαι δὲ καὶ τεταρταῖον, ἄδηλον γὰρ τοῦτο πρὸ τῆς πέμπτης, εἶτ’ ἐν τῇ τετάρτῃ τοῦ τε κατὰ τὴν πρώτην ἡμέραν ἀρξαμένου τεταρταίου [484] δεύτερον παροξυσμὸν, καὶ τοῦ κατὰ τὴν δευτέραν τριταίου δεύτερον.
english_sentence_A: It is possible, then, that the complication of the simple periods be of such a kind that on the first of the days a quotidian began; on the second, a tertian; on the third, possibly a tertian but possibly also a quartan—for this is unclear before the fifth day—and then that on the fourth day there be the second paroxysm of the quartan that began on the first day [484] and the second of the tertian that began on the second.
english_sentence_B: Now it is possible that the interweaving of the simple periods is also of this kind: that on the first of the days a quotidian began, and on the second a tertian; on the third it could be a tertian, and it could also be a quartan, for this is unclear before the fifth day; then on the fourth there would be the second paroxysm of the quartan that began on the first day [484], and the second of the tertian that began on the second.

english_sentence_B: How one ought to distinguish them, however, the [486] majority have not investigated at all, while some judge by the difference of the hours, as though it were not possible for all of them to make their onset, say, at the sixth hour, on different days. greek_sentence: καὶ πολλάκις ἐπὶ τῶν καμνόντων ἐθεασάμεθα δυοῖν τριταίοιν ἐπιπλοκὴν ἀμφημερινὸν ἕνα νομίζοντας εἶναι τοὺς θεραπεύοντας, οὓς μόγις ἐπείσαμεν ὑπὸ δυοῖν τριταίοιν ἐνοχλεῖσθαι τὸν κάμνοντα, λυθέντος μὲν ἐξ αὐτῶν πρότερον τοῦ προτέρου, καταλειφθέντος δὲ μόνου τοῦ χαλεπωτέρου.
english_sentence_A: And often in the case of the sick we have seen the attending physicians supposing a complication of two tertians to be a single quotidian, and we persuaded them only with difficulty that the patient was being troubled by two tertians, when the earlier of them had been resolved first and only the more severe one was left behind.
english_sentence_B: And often, in the case of patients, we have seen those treating them take an interweaving of two tertians to be a single quotidian. We had difficulty persuading them that the patient was afflicted by two tertians, until the earlier of the two had resolved first and only the more severe one remained.

greek_sentence: ἅπαντες οὖν ἐοίκασιν οἱ τὰ περὶ τύπων βιβλία γεγραφότες οὐδὲν φροντίσαι τῆς εἰς τὴν πρόγνωσίν τε καὶ δίαιταν ἐξ αὐτῶν ὠφελείας, ἀλλ’ ὥσπερ λέγουσιν, οὕτω καὶ ποιῆσαι, γυμνάσματα τοῖς νέοις γράψαι ταῦτα παραπλήσια τοῖς περὶ δεῖπνον αἰνίγμασιν, εἰ μὲν οὖν αὐτοὺς ἁπλῶς βούλονται γυμνάζειν, ἐνῆν τοῦτο πράττειν ἐπί τε γεωμετρίαν ἄγουσι καὶ ἀριθμητικὴν καὶ λογιστικὴν καὶ διαλεκτικήν· εἰ δ’ ἕνεκα τοῦ προγινώσκειν τὸν ἐρχόμενον παροξυσμὸν ἐπὶ τὸ γυμνάσιον ἀφικνοῦνται τοῦτο, τοῦ παντὸς ἁμαρτάνουσι, διὰ μοχθηρῶν ὁδῶν ἰέναι τοὺς νέους ἀναπείθοντες, [488] ἐξ ὧν οὐδὲν εὑρίσκουσιν οὔτ’ εἰς πρόγνωσιν οὔτ’ εἰς θεραπείαν χρηστὸν, ἐνὸν αὐτοὺς (ἑαυτοὺς) διδάξαι διαγινώσκειν παροξυσμὸν ἀμφημερινοῦ πυρετοῦ καὶ τριταίου καὶ τεταρταίου καὶ ἡμιτριταίου καὶ τριταιοφυοῦς, ἑκάστου τε τῶν ἄλλων, ὅσοι μὴ μόνον κατὰ τὸ σχῆμα τῶν περιόδων, ἀλλὰ καὶ κατὰ τὴν ὅλην φύσιν ἀλλήλοις διαφέρουσιν.
english_sentence_A: All those, then, who have written books on types seem to have given no thought at all to the benefit that may be drawn from them for prognosis and for regimen, but, just as they say, so too to have acted: they wrote these things as exercises for the young, resembling riddles posed at dinner. Now if they wish simply to exercise them, it was possible to do this by leading them to geometry and arithmetic and calculation and dialectic; but if it is for the sake of foreknowing the oncoming paroxysm that they come to this exercise, they miss the mark entirely, persuading the young to travel by bad roads, [488] from which they find nothing useful either for prognosis or for treatment, when it was possible for them to teach them (themselves) to diagnose the paroxysm of a quotidian fever and of a tertian and of a quartan and of a semitertian and of a tertian-natured fever, and that of each of the others, all those which differ from one another not only in the configuration of their periods but also in their whole nature.
english_sentence_B: All, then, who have written the books on types seem to have given no thought to the benefit to be had from them for prognosis and regimen, but, just as they themselves say, so also to have acted: to have written these things as exercises for the young, closely resembling the riddles posed at dinner. greek_sentence: ἅπαντες οὖν ἐοίκασιν οἱ τὰ περὶ τύπων βιβλία γεγραφότες οὐδὲν φροντίσαι τῆς εἰς τὴν πρόγνωσίν τε καὶ δίαιταν ἐξ αὐτῶν ὠφελείας, ἀλλ’ ὥσπερ λέγουσιν, οὕτω καὶ ποιῆσαι, γυμνάσματα τοῖς νέοις γράψαι ταῦτα παραπλήσια τοῖς περὶ δεῖπνον αἰνίγμασιν, εἰ μὲν οὖν αὐτοὺς ἁπλῶς βούλονται γυμνάζειν, ἐνῆν τοῦτο πράττειν ἐπί τε γεωμετρίαν ἄγουσι καὶ ἀριθμητικὴν καὶ λογιστικὴν καὶ διαλεκτικήν· εἰ δ’ ἕνεκα τοῦ προγινώσκειν τὸν ἐρχόμενον παροξυσμὸν ἐπὶ τὸ γυμνάσιον ἀφικνοῦνται τοῦτο, τοῦ παντὸς ἁμαρτάνουσι, διὰ μοχθηρῶν ὁδῶν ἰέναι τοὺς νέους ἀναπείθοντες, [488] ἐξ ὧν οὐδὲν εὑρίσκουσιν οὔτ’ εἰς πρόγνωσιν οὔτ’ εἰς θεραπείαν χρηστὸν, ἐνὸν αὐτοὺς (ἑαυτοὺς) διδάξαι διαγινώσκειν παροξυσμὸν ἀμφημερινοῦ πυρετοῦ καὶ τριταίου καὶ τεταρταίου καὶ ἡμιτριταίου καὶ τριταιοφυοῦς, ἑκάστου τε τῶν ἄλλων, ὅσοι μὴ μόνον κατὰ τὸ σχῆμα τῶν περιόδων, ἀλλὰ καὶ κατὰ τὴν ὅλην φύσιν ἀλλήλοις διαφέρουσιν.

english_sentence_A: For to those indeed who know how to recognise these, the whole theory about types is useless; and it would perhaps be better to say that this theory is entirely vain, whereas for him who has trained himself to recognise each of the fevers by its proper signs there is not only the gain of despising the vain nonsense, but also that of foreknowing the kind of regimen suited to each.
english_sentence_B: For to those at least who know how to recognise these, the whole theory of types is useless; or it might perhaps be better to say that this theory is wholly vain, and that for the man who has trained himself to recognise each of the fevers through its proper signs, the gain is not only to despise the vain babble, but also to foreknow the form of regimen suited to each.

greek_sentence: Ἐπεὶ δ’ ἠνάγκασάν μέ τινες τῶν νεωτέρων δεηθέντες, ἣν ἐγὼ παίζων αὐτοὺς ἐδίδαξα μέθοδον εἰς εὕρεσιν [489] τῶν ἐν ταῖς τοιαύταις ὑποθέσεσι τύπων, ἐν γράμμασι καταθέσθαι, δι’ ἐκείνους ἀνέθηκα καὶ τούτῳ τῷ λόγῳ μίαν ἡμέραν οὐχ ἑκών.
english_sentence_A: But since certain of the younger men, by their entreaties, compelled me to set down in writing the method which I had taught them in jest for the discovery [489] of the types in such problems, for their sake I have devoted a single day, not willingly, to this discourse as well.

greek_sentence: Ἐπεὶ δ’ ἠνάγκασάν μέ τινες τῶν νεωτέρων δεηθέντες, ἣν ἐγὼ παίζων αὐτοὺς ἐδίδαξα μέθοδον εἰς εὕρεσιν [489] τῶν ἐν ταῖς τοιαύταις ὑποθέσεσι τύπων, ἐν γράμμασι καταθέσθαι, δι’ ἐκείνους ἀνέθηκα καὶ τούτῳ τῷ λόγῳ μίαν ἡμέραν οὐχ ἑκών.

lsj_entry_text: ἑκών, ἑκοῦσα, ἑκόν: ( vέκ- IG 9(1).334.12 ( Locr. ), GDI 5131b (Crete), cf. γεκαθά; cf. Skt. váśmi 'wish'):—readily, Od. 4.649 , etc.; freq. contrasted with ἄκων, ἑ. ἀέκοντί γε θυμῷ Il. 4.43 ; οὐ γάρ τίς με βίῃ γε ἑ. ἀέκοντα δίηται 7.197 ; ἑκόνθ' ἑκόντι Ζηνὶ συμπαραστατεῖν A. lsj_entry_text: ἕκαστος, η, ον, each, opp. the whole body, Il. 2.805 , etc. : sg. with pl. Verb, ἔβαν οἶκόνδε ἕκαστος they went home each to his own house, 1.606 ; δεδμήμεσθα ἕκαστος 5.878 , cf. Hdt. 3.158 ; so in Att. , Ar. Pl. 785 , Pl. Prt. 327e , etc. ; ὅτι ἕκαστος ἐπίστασθε ἀγαθόν X. Smp. 3.3 : sg. in apposition with pl. Noun or Pron., which expresses the whole, Τρῶας δὲ τρόμος αἰνὸς ὑπήλυθε γυῖα ἕκαστον Il. 7.215 ; ὔμμι..ἑκάστῳ 15.109 ; αἱ δὲ γυναῖκες..θαύμαζον..ἑκάστη 18.496 , etc. ; Περσίδες δ'.. ἑκάστα..λείπεται A. Pers. 135 (lyr.) ; αἱ ἄλλαι πᾶσαι [τέχναι] τὸ αὑτῆς ἑκάστη ἔργον ἐργάζεται Pl. R. 346d , cf. Grg. 503e ; ὅστις ἕκαστος every one which.. (nisi leg. ὥς τις), Hes. Th. 459 . the Art. is sts. added to the Subst. (so regularly in earlier Att. Inscrr., IG 12.22.14 , al., exc. ἑκάστου μηνός ib. 6.125 ) with which ἕκαστος agrees, in which case ἕκαστος is commonly put first, καθ' ἑ. τὴν ἡμέραν every single day, Isoc. 12.211 , etc. ; περὶ ἑ. τῆς τέχνης Pl. Phdr. 274e : also following the Subst., κατὰ τὸν οξπλίτην ἕκαστον Th. 5.49 ; κατὰ τὴν ἡμέραν ἑκάστην Id. 6.63 , al. in pl., all and each severally, Il. 1.550 , al., A. Supp. 932 , etc. ; οἷστισιν ἑκάστοις to whichsoever severally, Pl. Lg. 799a . each of two or more groups or parties, Od. 9.164 , Hdt. 1.169 , A. Pr. 491 , Th. 6.77 , etc. strengthd. by the addition of other Prons., εἷς ἕ. (v. εἷς) ; εἷς τις ἕ. S. Ant. 262 ; ἕκαστός τις each one, Pi. N. 4.92 , Th. 3.45 , etc. ; ταῦτα ἕκαστα Hdt. 5.13 , etc. ; αὔθ' ἕκαστα all in exact detail, A. Pr. 950 . with Preps., esp. κατά, καθ' ἕκαστον singly, by itself, Pl. Tht. 188a , al. ; καθ' ἕ. καὶ σύμπαντα Id. Sph. 259b ; τὸ καθ' ἕ., τὰ καθ' ἕκαστα, particulars, Arist. Ph. 189a6 , EN 1143b4 , al. ; παρ' ἕκαστον, παρ' ἕκαστα, in every case, Plb. 4.82.5 , 3.57.4 , etc. ; παρ' ἕκαστον καὶ ἔργον καὶ λόγον διδάσκοντες Pl. P. 9.98 ; οὐχ ὡς ἕ. ἀλλὰπάντες Arist. Pol. 1292a12 , cf. 1283b34 . later, = ἑκάτερος , D.H. 3.2 codd. ( vέκαστος Leg.Gort. 1.9 , al., Schwyzer 409.4 (Elis), IG 9(1).334.9 (Locris). greek_sentence: τύπον οὗτοι καλοῦσιν οὐχ ἅπασαν περίοδον, ἀλλ’ ἥτις ἂν ἐξ ὁλοκλήρων ἡμερῶν τε καὶ νυκτῶν συγκέηται, καὶ καθ’ ἕκαστόν γε πλῆθος ἡμερῶν ἴδιον εἶναι βούλονται τύπον, οὐδὲ κ΄ ἢ λ΄ μόνον ἡμερῶν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τούτων ἐξωτέρω τὰς τῶν τύπων περιόδους ἐκτείνοντες.
english_sentence_A: These men call a type not every period, but whichever one is composed of whole days and nights, and for each number of days they maintain that there is a distinct type, extending the periods of the types not only to twenty or thirty days, but even beyond these.
english_sentence_B: These men call a 'type' not every period, but only that which is composed of whole days and nights, and they would have each number of days be its own type, extending the periods of the types not merely to 20 or 30 days, but even beyond these.

greek_sentence: τὸν ἀριθμὸν τῶν ὡρῶν ἑκάστου τύπου πρόχειρον ﻿ [490] ἔχειν προσῆκεν ἤτοι διὰ μνήμης, ἢ γεγραμμένον ἐν χαρτίῳ, τοῦ μὲν ἀμφημερινοῦ τὸν τῶν κδ΄, τριταίου δὲ τὸν τῶν ὀκτὼ καὶ τετταράκοντα, καὶ οὕτως ἐφεξῆς, τεταρταίου μὲν οβ΄, πεμπταίου δὲ νστ΄, ἑκταίου ρκ΄, ἑβδομαίου δὲ ρμδ΄ καὶ τῶν ἄλλων, ὡς τοῦτο τὸ διάγραμμα τὸ ὑποτεταγμένον ἔχει.

english_sentence_A: And after the preparation of this, let them examine of which of the numbers written first the proposed paroxysm of the periodic hours according to the paroxysms is a part.

greek_sentence: εἰ μὲν γὰρ τρίτον εἴη τὸ μόριον ὁ κατὰ τὴν περίοδον ἀριθμὸς τῶν ὡρῶν τοῦ τύπου, τρεῖς ἐρεῖς ἀλλήλοις ἐκείνους περιπεπλέχθαι τοὺς τύπους· εἰ δὲ τέταρτον, τέτταρας· εἰ δὲ πέμπτον, πέντε, παρώνυμον ἀεὶ τὸν ἀριθμὸν τοῦ μέρους ποιούμενος.
english_sentence_A: For having found it, they will have the genus of the type (whether one says genus, or species, or form, or nature will make no difference in the present case), and the number of the types that have been found, according to the part. For if the part should be a third, that is, the number of the hours of the type in the period, you will say that three of those types are intertwined with one another; if a fourth, four; if a fifth, five, always making the number derive its name from the part.
english_sentence_B: For when they have found it, they will have the genus of the type (whether one says genus, or species, or form, or nature makes no difference for the present), and they will have the number of the types found from the fraction. For if the number of the hours of the type in its period should be a third as its fraction, you will say that those types are three, intertwined with one another; if a fourth, four; if a fifth, five, always making the number paronymous with the part.

For if the part should be a third, that is, the number of the hours of the type in the period, you will say that three of those types are intertwined with one another; if a fourth, four; if a fifth, five, always making the number derive its name from the part.
english_sentence_B: For when they have found it, they will have the genus of the type (whether one says genus, or species, or form, or nature makes no difference for the present), and they will have the number of the types found from the fraction. greek_sentence: ἵνα δὲ καὶ διὰ παραδείγματος εὑρεθῇ σαφεστέρα ἡ μέθοδος, ἔστω τινὰ παροξύνεσθαι μὲν ὥραις στ΄, ἐξανίεσθαι δὲ δυοῖν, ὥστε τὴν ὅλην περίοδον ὑπάρχειν ὡρῶν ὀκτώ· κατὰ ταύτην τὴν ὑπόθεσιν [494] ἐπισκέψῃ, τί μέρος ἐστὶ τὰ η΄ τῶν κδ΄, εἶθ’ εὑρὼν ὅτι τρίτον, ἀμφημερινοὺς ἐρεῖς ἐπιπεπλέχθαι τρεῖς· ἀμφημερινοὺς μὲν, ὅτι τοῦ τῶν κδ΄ ἀριθμοῦ μόριόν ἐστιν ὁ τῶν ὀκτώ· τρεῖς δὲ, ὅτι τρίτον.
english_sentence_A: But so that the method may also be found clearer by means of an example, let someone have a paroxysm for six hours and a remission for two, so that the whole period is of eight hours. On this hypothesis [494] you will examine what part eight is of twenty-four; then, having found that it is a third, you will say that three quotidians are interwoven: quotidians, because the number eight is a part of the number twenty-four; three, because it is a third.
english_sentence_B: And so that the method may be found clearer also by means of an example, let someone be in paroxysm for 6 hours and in remission for two, so that the whole period is one of eight hours. On this hypothesis [494] you will examine what part the 8 are of the 24; then, having found that it is a third, you will say that three quotidians are interwoven: quotidians, because the number eight is a part of the number 24; three, because it is a third.

greek_sentence: ἀεὶ τοίνυν εὑρεθήσεταί σοι τὸ μὲν εἶδος τῶν τύπων ἐκ τῶν ἐν τῷ διαγράμματι γεγραμμένων [496] ἀριθμῶν· τὸ δὲ πλῆθος αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ γνῶναι πόστον ἐστὶ τὸ τοῦ ἀριθμοῦ μέρος ὁ τῶν κατὰ τοὺς παροξυσμοὺς ὡρῶν ἀριθμὸς, ὅπερ ταὐτόν ἐστι τῷ γνῶναι κατὰ τίνα τῶν ἀριθμῶν ὁ κατὰ τοὺς παροξυσμοὺς μετρεῖ τὸν τοῦ τύπου· παρονομάζονται γὰρ ἀλλήλοις ὅ τ’ ἀριθμὸς οὗτος καὶ τὸ μόριον.
english_sentence_A: Always, therefore, the species of the types will be found by you from the numbers written in the diagram; [496] and their number (multitude) from knowing what fraction of the number the number of the hours at the paroxysms is, which is the same as knowing according to which of the numbers the number at the paroxysms measures that of the type; for this number and the part are named after one another.
english_sentence_B: You will therefore always find the kind of the types from the numbers written in the diagram [496], and their number from knowing what fraction of the number the number of the hours of the paroxysms is. This is the same as knowing according to which of the numbers the number of the paroxysms measures that of the type, for this number and the part are named after one another.

greek_sentence: ἀλλ’ ἐγὼ μὲν ἀντὶ παιδείας ἕκαστον τούτων ἀποκρίνομαι τοῖς προλαβοῦσι παραχρῆμα, διὰ τὸ γεγυμνάσθαι τὴν παιδικὴν ἡλικίαν ἐν ἀριθμοῖς· ἀγύμναστος δὲ ἄνθρωπος οὐ μηνῶν, ἀλλ’ ἐτῶν ὅλων εἰς αὐτοὺς δεῖται χάριν τοῦ γενέσθαι σοφὸς ἐν ἀχρήστοις πράγμασιν, ἃ μετὰ σπουδῆς τινες ἀλλήλοις προβάλλοντες οὐκ αἰδοῦνται.
english_sentence_A: But I for my part, in virtue of my education, answer each of these on the spot to those who put them to me, because I was exercised in numbers in my boyhood years; whereas an unexercised man needs not months but whole years for them, in order to become wise in useless matters, which some are not ashamed to propose to one another with earnest zeal.
english_sentence_B: But I, by way of a pastime, answer each of these on the spot to those who put them to me first, because I was trained in numbers from childhood. An untrained man, however, needs not months but whole years for them, in order to become wise in useless matters, which some people are not ashamed to propose to one another in earnest.

greek_sentence: ὅτι μὲν οὖν ἁμαρτάνουσι διττὰ πάντες οἱ τὰ περὶ τύπων ὑπομνήματα γράψαντες, οὔτε τὰς ἰδέας τῶν νοσημάτων διδάσκοντες οὔτε τοῖς εὐχρήστοις τρίβοντες τὸν χρόνον, αὐτάρκως ἡγοῦμαι δεδεῖχθαι.
english_sentence_A: That, then, all who have written treatises on types err in a twofold way, neither teaching the forms of the diseases nor spending their time on useful things, I consider to have been sufficiently shown.
english_sentence_B: That all those who wrote treatises on types err in two ways, neither teaching the forms of the diseases nor spending their time on useful things, I think has been sufficiently shown.

greek_sentence: Ἐπεὶ δ’ ἠνάγκασαν ἡμᾶς ἐάσαντας χρήσιμα τὸν χρόνον εἰς τὴν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἀντιλογίαν ἀναλίσκειν, ἐπιδείξωμεν αὐτοῖς, εἰς ὅσον ἀναισθησίας ἥκουσιν αὐτοί τε καὶ οἱ προσέχοντες αὐτοῖς, ὥς τι διδάσκουσι χρήσιμον.
english_sentence_A: But since they have compelled us to leave aside useful things and expend our time on the refutation directed against them, let us demonstrate to them to what degree of insensibility they have come, both they themselves and those who attend to them as though they were teaching something useful.
english_sentence_B: But since they have compelled us to leave useful things aside and spend our time on the refutation of them, let us show them to what a degree of obtuseness they have come, both they themselves and those who attend to them as though they taught something useful.

english_sentence_A: For although they themselves admit [500] that their discussions are about an impossible matter, nevertheless, handling them as a kind of exercise, why on earth do they not exercise themselves in even the thousandth part of the whole of treatment—in addition to the fact that their hypotheses also conflict with one another, which I shall go through for you first?
english_sentence_B: For although they themselves have admitted [500] that their discussions concern a thing that is impossible, and nevertheless handle them as a kind of exercise, why on earth do they not exercise themselves in even the thousandth part of the whole of therapy? greek_sentence: ἐγὼ δὲ τίνα μὲν ἔχω γνώμην ὑπὲρ ὧν Ἱπποκράτης εἶπεν ἐξωτέρω τῆς τοῦ τεταρταίου περιόδου, ἐν ἑτέροις ἐδήλωσα, δι’ ὧν ἐδίδασκον, ὡς ἐμαυτὸν πείθω, θεωρίαν χρήσιμον τῇ τέχνῃ· νυνὶ δὲ, οὐ γὰρ διδάξαι μοί τι πρόκειται κατὰ τόνδε τὸν λόγον, ἀλλ’ ἐξελέγξαι τοὺς μήτε τὰ χρήσιμα γράφοντας ἐπαινοῦντάς τε θεωρίαν ἀχρηστοτάτην, ἐπὶ πρώτους τρέψομαι τοὺς ἄχρι τοῦ πεντεκαιδεκαταίου τύπου γυμνασίας ἕνεκα προϊέναι φάσκοντας.
english_sentence_A: As for the opinion I hold concerning what Hippocrates said about what lies beyond the period of the quartan, I have made it clear in other writings, in which I taught, as I persuade myself, a theory useful to the art; but now—for it is not my purpose in this discourse to teach anything, but to refute those who do not write what is useful and who praise a most useless theory—I shall turn first to those who say that, for the sake of exercise, they proceed as far as the fifteen-day type.
english_sentence_B: What opinion I hold about the things Hippocrates said beyond the quartan period I have made clear elsewhere, in works in which I was teaching, as I persuade myself, a theory useful to the art. But now, since it is not my purpose in this treatise to teach anything, but to refute those who neither write what is useful and who praise a most useless theory, I shall turn first to those who claim that they proceed as far as the fifteenth-day type for the sake of exercise.

( = ἡ δοθεῖσα ) the constitution based on a presupposition, ib. 1288b28 ; of currency, ἓν δή τι δεῖ εἶναι, τοῦτο δ' ἐξ ὑ.· διὸ νόμισμα καλεῖται according to a presupposed convention, Id. EE 1227a8 , cf. b30 ; τῶν πράξεων τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ὑ. ἀληθεῖς καὶ δικαίας εἶναι προσήκει D. 2.10 ; of a thing, that without which it cannot exist or be what it is, its essence, αὕτη (sc. τὸ στέλεχος) οἷον ὑ. καὶ φύσις δένδρων Thphr. APo. 81b15 ; ὅσα δέδεικται δι' ἐκείνων ὑποθέσεις ποιησάμενοι taking as premisses (here) what has been proved in those other works, Gal. 6.7 , cf. 25 , 224 ; ἴστω . . τῆς ὑγιεινῆς πραγματείας ἀνατρέπων τὴν ὑ. ib. 17 ; ὑπόθεσιν, αἴτησιν οὖσαν πράγματος εἰς κατασκευήν τινος S.E. lsj_entry_text: ἀμφημερινὸς πυρετός, quotidian fever, opp. τριταῖος and τεταρταῖος, Hp. Epid. 1.6 , Pl. Ti. 86a : neut. as Adv., -νὸν πυρεταίνειν Aret. SD 1.2 :—also ἀμφελυτρ-ήμερος (sc. πυρετός), S. Fr. 507 .
greek_sentence: εἰ γὰρ ὁ διὰ κ΄ καὶ γ΄ ὡρῶν παροξυνόμενος πυρετὸς οὐκ ἔστιν ἀμφημερινὸς προληπτικὸς, ἀναγκαῖον αὐτὸν εἶναι τέτταρας [501] καὶ εἴκοσιν εἰκοστοτεταρταίους· ὥσπερ οὖν καὶ τὸν ὑστεροῦντα μίαν ὥραν εἰκοστοεκταίους εἶναι καὶ τοῦτο κ΄ τε καὶ τέτταρας.
english_sentence_A: For if the fever that has its paroxysm every twenty-three hours is not an anticipating quotidian, it is necessary that it be twenty-four [501] twenty-fourth-day fevers; just as, likewise, the one that lags by one hour must be twenty-sixth-day fevers, and these too twenty-four in number.
english_sentence_B: For if the fever that has its paroxysm every twenty-three hours is not an anticipating quotidian, it must necessarily be four [501] and twenty twenty-fourth-day fevers; just as, then, the one that is late by one hour must also be twenty-sixth-day fevers, and this too twenty and four of them.

lsj_entry_text: τέσσαρες, οἱ, αἱ , τέσσαρα, τά , gen. ων: dat. τέσσαρσι(ν) Th. 2.21 , Act.Ap. 12.4 , etc.; poet. τέτρασι Hes. Fr. 188 , Pi. lsj_entry_text: εἴκοσι (for εἴκοσιν v. infr.), Att. , Ion. , also Arc., IG 5(2).3.1 (Tegea), and Aeol. , ib. 12(2).6.21 (Lesbos):—indecl., twenty, Il. 2.510 , 748 , etc.; in Hom. more freq. in Ep. form ἐείκοσι, before a vowel ἐείκοσιν, 1.309 , 6.217 , al.; Dor. vίκατι Leg.Gort. 4.13 , etc.; vείκατι Tab.Heracl. 2.71 ; Lacon. βείκατι Hsch. ; εἴκατι IG 9(1).693.10 (Corc.), Theoc. 4.10 , 5.86 . (Orig. vίκατι and Ἐvίκοσι, whence ἐείκοσι in Hom. ; vείκατι and εἴκατι are late spellings of (v)ίκατι; εἴκοσι is contr. from Ἐvίκοσι. Cf. Lat. vīginti, Skt. viṃśatis. εἴκοσιν is the only form used by Ar. , whether before vowels or consonants (εἴκοσ' ἀπολογίζεται is dub. in Fr. 465 ); also (before consonants) Herod. 3.91 , Phld. Piet. 3 , etc., but not common in Inscrr. or Pap., e.g. (before consonants) Schwyzer 707 B 2 (Ephesus, vi B. C.), IG 2.804.155 (iv B.C.), (before a vowel) PGrenf. 2.75.7 (iv A. D.); εἴκοσι ἔτη, εἴκοσι ἡμερῶν, IG 12.94 , 49 .)
greek_sentence: εἰ γὰρ ὁ διὰ κ΄ καὶ γ΄ ὡρῶν παροξυνόμενος πυρετὸς οὐκ ἔστιν ἀμφημερινὸς προληπτικὸς, ἀναγκαῖον αὐτὸν εἶναι τέτταρας [501] καὶ εἴκοσιν εἰκοστοτεταρταίους· ὥσπερ οὖν καὶ τὸν ὑστεροῦντα μίαν ὥραν εἰκοστοεκταίους εἶναι καὶ τοῦτο κ΄ τε καὶ τέτταρας.
english_sentence_A: For if the fever that has its paroxysm every twenty-three hours is not an anticipating quotidian, it is necessary that it be twenty-four [501] twenty-fourth-day fevers; just as, likewise, the one that lags by one hour must be twenty-sixth-day fevers, and these too twenty-four in number.
english_sentence_B: For if the fever that has its paroxysm every twenty-three hours is not an anticipating quotidian, it must necessarily be four [501] and twenty twenty-fourth-day fevers; just as, then, the one that is late by one hour must also be twenty-sixth-day fevers, and this too twenty and four of them.

D), and in good codd. of Arist. IA 704a11 , al., Theol.Ar. 19 , etc.; also τέταρσι SIG 729.3 (Delph., i B.C.), PSI 9.1028.10 (i A.D.):— Att. τέτταρες, τέτταρα, dat. τέτταρσιν Isoc. 12.3 ; also τάρων (v. τάρες) for τεττάρων; Phocian dat. τεττάροις IG 9(1).32.78 (Stiris, ii B.C.):— Ion. and later Gr. τέσσερες, τέσσερα, SIG 57.25 (Milet., v B.C.), Schwyzer 289.120 (Rhodian, ii B.C.), etc. (dat. τέσσερσι Hdt. 6.41 , τεσσέρασιν SIG 633.98 (Milet., ii B.C.)), but τέσσαρες in Hom. , and Schwyzer 707 B 4 (Ephesus, vi B.C.), etc.: codd. of LXX have τέσσαρες (nom. and acc.), τεσσάρων, τέσσαρσι, but τέσσερἁσʼ, τεσσεράκοντα; since however τέσσερα(ς) and τεσσεράκοντα, apart from Ion. , are not common in Papyri before ii A.D., the LXX autographs prob. had τέσσαρα(ς) and τεσσαράκοντα; the form τέσσερα(ς) is here due to avoidance by the copyists of the sequence ε-α-α:— Dor. τέτορες, τέτορα, Hes. Op. 698 , Phoc. 3 , Simon. 91 , Epich. 149 , SIG 240 I 8 (Delph., iv B.C.), al., Theoc. 14.16 :— Ep. (prob. Aeol. ) πίσυρες [ι] Od. 5.70 , 16.249 , A.R. 2.1110 , Nic. D. 16.119 , 38.176 , 236 , 39.377 , AP 14.7.4 : Aeol. also πέσυρες, neut. πέσυρα Epigr.Gr. 988.6 (Balbilla); and πέσσυρες, πέσσυρα, Hsch. :— Boeot. πέτταρες, α (q.v.):—four, Od. 9.335 , etc.; διὰ τεττάρων the musical interval of the fourth, Damox. 2.55 , etc.; τὰ τέσσαρα the four simple bodies of Empedocles, Plot. 6.2.2 ; the four kinds of quality or four Aristotelian senses of ποιόν, Id. 6.1.10 ; the four cardinal principles of Epicurus (cf. τετραφάρμακος), Phld. english_sentence_A: And much more so when they reduce a tertian or quartan or indeed quintan period that lags or anticipates by two or three hours to combinations of types, in the same way as the twenty-four twenty-sixth-day fevers.

greek_sentence: ἵνα γὰρ ἐάσας τὴν πεντεκαίδεχ’ ἡμερῶν αὐτῶν περίοδον, ἐπὶ τὴν τοῦ πεμπταίου παραγένωμαι, κατὰ τοῦτον τὸν τύπον, ἐὰν μὲν προλάβῃ μίαν ὥραν ὁ παροξυσμὸς, εἴκοσι καὶ τέτταρες ἐννενηκονθεκταῖοι γενήσονται· ἐὰν δὲ ὑστερίζῃ, ἐννενηκοστοογδαῖοι πάλιν κδ΄, εἰ δ΄ αὐτὰ δὴ ὑποτίθενταί τινας ἤδη προλαμβάνοντας καὶ ὑστερίζοντας, ἀναιροῦσιν ἄρδην ἑαυτῶν τὴν ὑπόθεσιν.
english_sentence_A: For—leaving aside their period of fifteen days, so as to come to that of the quintan—in the case of this type, if the paroxysm anticipates by one hour, there will come to be twenty-four ninety-sixth-day fevers; and if it lags, again twenty-four ninety-eighth-day fevers. But if they themselves (αὐτὰ) do in fact posit these very things, certain fevers that already anticipate and lag, they utterly abolish their own hypothesis.
english_sentence_B: For, to leave aside their fifteen-day period and come to that of the quintan: in this type, if the paroxysm anticipates by one hour, there will come to be twenty-four ninety-sixth-day fevers; and if it is late, again twenty-four ninety-eighth-day fevers. But if they suppose these very things, namely that some already anticipate and are late, they utterly destroy their own hypothesis.

english_sentence_A: For even if they say nothing else, they at least neatly escape the counter-argument against them, and are not, like the former, overthrown by their own selves, positing that the types proceed as far as fifteen days, yet being compelled to make use not only of those composed of many tens, but also of those composed of hundreds.

greek_sentence: ἐπεὶ τοίνυν ἀδύνατόν ἐστιν αὐτοῖς φυγεῖν τὸ πλῆθος τῶν τύπων, ἀδύνατον δήπου καὶ τὰς ἐπιπλοκὰς ἀλλήλοις ἐπιπλέκοντας φεύγειν· ἀλλὰ καθάπερ οἱ τοὺς τρεῖς τύπους ὑποθέμενοι μόνους ὑπάρχειν, ἀμφημερινὸν καὶ τριταῖον καὶ τεταρταῖον, ὅμως ἐκ τῆς ἐπιπλοκῆς αὐτῶν συζυγίας ἀποτελοῦσι πολλὰς, οὕτως ἀναγκαῖον ἔσται καὶ τούτοις ἐπιπλέκειν ἀλλήλοις ἅπαντας τοὺς τύπους.
english_sentence_A: Since, then, it is impossible for them to escape the multitude of types, it is surely impossible also to escape the complications when they interweave them with one another; but just as those who posited that only three types exist, the quotidian, the tertian and the quartan, nevertheless produce many conjunctions from their complication, so it will be necessary for these too to interweave all the types with one another.
english_sentence_B: Since, then, it is impossible for them to escape the multitude of types, it is surely impossible for them also to escape the interlacings, as they interlace the types with one another. Rather, just as those who posit that only the three types exist, quotidian, tertian and quartan, nevertheless produce many pairings from their interlacing, so it will be necessary for these men too to interlace all the types with one another.

english_sentence_A: Let us begin, then, from the quintan, and show them how, being interwoven with this one, it will produce a great many conjunctions, it making no difference whether someone should name them not conjunctions but complications.

greek_sentence: μία μὲν γὰρ ἡ συζυγία τοιαύτη· τῇ πρώτῃ τῶν ἡμερῶν ἀρχέσθω πεμπταῖος, [503] εἶθ’ ἡ τρίτη τε καὶ τετάρτη καθαρευέτω πυρετοῦ παντός· ἡ πέμπτη μὲν τοῦ κατὰ τὴν πρώτην ἡμέραν ἀρξαμένου πεμπταίου τὸν δεύτερον ἐχέτω παροξυσμὸν, ἡ δ’ ἕκτη τοῦ κατὰ τὴν δευτέραν· εἶτα τῆς ζ΄ καὶ τῆς η΄ καθαρευουσῶν, ἡ μὲν ἐννάτη τὸν τρίτον ἐχέτω παροξυσμὸν τοῦ πρώτου τῶν πεμπταίων, ἡ δὲ δεκάτη τοῦ δευτέρου καὶ αὐτὴ τὸν τρίτον ἐφεξῆς· καὶ κατὰ τὴν αὐτὴν ἀναλογίαν ὁ τέταρτος πεμπταῖος προερχέσθω, διαφέροντος οὐδὲν εἰς τὰ παρόντα, διπλοῦν πεμπταῖον ἢ δύο πεμπταίους λέγειν, ὅπερ οὐδ’ αὐτὸ συγχωροῦσιν ἅπαντες.
english_sentence_A: For one conjunction is of this sort: let a quintan begin on the first of the days, [503] then let the third and the fourth be clear of all fever; let the fifth have the second paroxysm of the quintan that began on the first day, and the sixth that of the one on the second; then, the seventh and the eighth being clear, let the ninth have the third paroxysm of the first of the quintans, and the tenth, in its turn, the third paroxysm of the second in sequence; and in the same proportion let the fourth quintan proceed, it making no difference for the present purpose whether one speaks of a double quintan or of two quintans, which point itself not everyone concedes.
english_sentence_B: For one combination is of this kind: on the first of the days let a quintan begin, [503] then let the third and the fourth be clear of all fever; let the fifth have the second paroxysm of the quintan that began on the first day, and the sixth that of the one that began on the second; then, the seventh and the eighth being clear, let the ninth have the third paroxysm of the first of the quintans, and the tenth that of the second, this too being its third in sequence; and in the same proportion let the fourth quintan proceed, it making no difference for present purposes whether one speaks of a double quintan or of two quintans, a point which not everyone concedes either.

Hipp. 1131 (lyr.); of persons, Plu. Demetr. 1 : generally, pair, Pl. Phd. 71c , Prm. 143d , Arist. IA 704b20 ; ς. πτερύγων, μήλων, δονάκων, AP 5.267.6 , 289 (both Paul. Sil.), 6.27 ( Theaet. ); ἄρσενα ς., of two sons, IG 12(8).442.6 (Thasos); κατὰ συζυγίας in pairs, esp. of animals, κατὰ συζυγίας φωλοῦσιν . . οἱ ἄρρενες θήλεσιν Arist. HA 599b6 , cf. 631b1 ; in plants, Thphr. HP 3.11.3 , al.: hence, coupling, copulation, AP 5.220 (Paul. Sil.), 10.68 ( Agath. ). in war, squadron of four war-chariots,= two ζυγαρχίαι, Ascl. Tact. 8 , Ael. Tact. 22.2 . conjunction of words or things in pairs, syzygy, Arist. Top. 113a12 , GC 332b3 (pl.), Mete. 378b11 (pl.), Stoic. 2.132 , Gal. 6.95 , al.: more generally, combination of words, οὐκ ἐν τῷ κάλλει τῶν ὀνομάτων ἡ πειθώ, ἀλλ' ἐν τῇ ς. D.H. Comp. 3 , cf. 6 ; of letters, ib. 22 ; coupling of terms in a syllogism, Chrysipp.Stoic. 2.50 . Gramm., conjugation, D.T. 638.6 (pl.), A.D. Adv. 161.28 , POxy. 469.13 (iii A.D.); or declension, A.D. Adv. 198.6 , Synt. 271.16 , Ath. 9.392b ; any group of related words, e.g. sapiens, sapienter, sapientia, Cic. Top. 3.12 , cf. 9.38 . in Prosody, syzygy, dipodia, Heph. 7.8 , Aristid. Quint. 1.14 , Syrian. in Hermog. 1p.31R. syncope, Anon.Rhythm. 3.19 . Astron., syzygy, of two stars one of which rises and sets as the other sets and rises, Autol. 1.4 ; of zodiacal signs rising and setting between the same points of the horizon, Gem. 2.27 ; of the moon's conjunctions and oppositions with the sun, Ptol. Alm. 5.1 , Cat.Cod.Astr. 1.131 ; so of planets, Ptol. Alm. 5.10 . greek_sentence: ἐὰν οὖν οὕτως ἐπιπλέξωμεν αὐτῷ καὶ τὸν ἑκταῖον, εὔδηλον ὡς πλείους αἱ συζυγίαι γενήσονται· καὶ πλείους ἔτι, τὸν ἑβδομαῖον ἐπιπλεκόντων, καὶ πολὺ πλείους ἔτι τὸν ὀγδοαῖον, ἢ καὶ τὸν δεκαταῖον, ἵνα μηδὲν εἴπω περὶ τῶν εἰκοσταίων καὶ τριακοσταίων καὶ τεσσαρακοσταίων, ὅσοι τε πρὸς τούτοις ἐδείχθησαν ἐξ ἀνάγκης ἑπόμενοι ταῖς ὑποθέσεσιν αὐτῶν.
english_sentence_A: If, then, we interweave with it in this way the sextan as well, it is quite evident that the combinations will become more numerous; and more numerous still when one interweaves the septan, and far more numerous still the octan, or indeed the decan—to say nothing of the twenty-day, thirty-day and forty-day fevers, and all those which, in addition to these, have been shown to follow of necessity from their hypotheses.
english_sentence_B: If, then, in this way we also interweave the sextan with it, it is quite clear that the combinations will become more numerous; and more numerous still if we interweave the septan, and much more numerous still the octan, or even the decan, not to speak of the twentieth-day, thirtieth-day and fortieth-day fevers, and all those besides that were shown to follow of necessity from their hypotheses.

greek_sentence: κᾀμοὶ πρῶτον ἐννόησον, ὡς νῦν ὁπότε διπλοῦς ὁ πεμπταῖος γίγνεται, τὰς συζυγίας εἴπομεν, ἐὰν δὲ τριπλοῦς γενηθείη, δῆλον ὅτι πλῆθος οὐκ ὀλίγον ἄλλο γίνεται συζυγιῶν.
english_sentence_A: And consider first, for my sake, that we have now stated the combinations for the case when the quintan becomes double; but if it should become triple, it is clear that another not small multitude of combinations arises.
english_sentence_B: And first consider with me that we have now stated the combinations for when the quintan becomes double; but if it should become triple, it is clear that another multitude of combinations, and no small one, arises.

greek_sentence: ἐγχωρεῖ δήπου καὶ τετραπλοῦν αὐτὸν γενέσθαι, καθ’ ἑκάστην ἡμέραν ﻿ [505] ἑνὸς εἰσβάλλοντος παροξυσμοῦ· πενταπλοῦς δ’ ἂν γένοιτο μιχθέντος τῷ τετραπλῷ κατὰ μίαν νύκτα πέμπτου τινὸς ἐπὶ τοῖς εἰρημένοις τέτταρσι πεμπταίοις, καὶ τούτου πάλιν αὐτοῦ τετραχῶς· ἢ γὰρ ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ νυκτὶ τὴν ἀρχὴν δύναται λαβεῖν, ἤ τινι τῶν ἐφεξῆς, ἤτοι τῇ δευτέρᾳ, ἢ τῇ τρίτῃ, ἢ τῇ τετάρτῃ, ἢ τῇ πέμπτῃ.
english_sentence_A: It is surely possible for it to become fourfold as well, with one paroxysm attacking on each day; [505] and it would become fivefold if some fifth one were mixed with the fourfold in a single night, in addition to the four quintans mentioned, and this again itself in four ways; for it can take its beginning either in the first night or in one of the following ones, namely the second, or the third, or the fourth, or the fifth.
english_sentence_B: It is surely possible for it also to become fourfold, with, on each day, [505] one paroxysm setting in; and it would become fivefold if, along with the fourfold, some fifth were mixed in during one night in addition to the four quintans mentioned, and this one again in four ways (τετραχῶς); for it can take its beginning either on the first night or on one of those following, that is, on the second, or the third, or the fourth, or the fifth.

greek_sentence: ἡ δ’ αὐτὴ ποικίλη τούτοις ἐστὶ καὶ τοὺς ἄλλους τύπους, καὶ μᾶλλον ἔτι κατὰ τοὺς πολυημερωτέρους αὐτῶν.
english_sentence_A: The same variety exists in the case of these also for the other types, and still more in the case of those of them that extend over more days.

greek_sentence: ἐὰν οὖν ἐπιπλέκῃς ἅπασαν τὴν τοῦ πεμπταίου ποικιλίαν τῇ κατὰ τὸν ἑκταῖον, ἐννοεῖς, οἶμαι, πόσον ἔσται πλῆθος· ἐὰν δὲ μίξῃς αὐταῖς καὶ τὸν ἑβδομαῖον, ἢ ὀγδοαῖον, ἤ τινα τῶν ἐφεξῆς, εἶτα πάλιν ἐκ τεττάρων τύπων οὕτως ἀλλήλοις ἐπιπεπλεγμένων ἑτέρας ποιήσῃς συζυγίας, εἶτ’ ἐκ πέντε, κᾄπειτ’ αὖθις ἐκ πλειόνων, οἶμαί σε λογίζεσθαι πόσος ἀριθμὸς ἔσται συζυγιῶν, ἢ πόσων δεήσει βιβλίων εἰς τὴν διδασκαλίαν αὐτῶν.

greek_sentence: καθ’ ἕκαστον τῶν τύπων πρότερον δεήσει τὴν ποικιλίαν τῶν συζυγιῶν διελθεῖν, ὡς ἐπὶ τοῦ πεμπταίου σμικρὸν ἔμπροσθεν ἔδειξα· μετὰ ταῦτα ἐπιπλέκειν ἀλλήλαις αὐτὰς, [506] πρῶτον μὲν μίαν συζυγίαν τῶν ἐκ τοῦ πεμπταίου, φέρε εἰπεῖν, μιᾷ τῇ κατὰ τὸν ἑκταῖον, ὡς ἐκ δυοῖν συζυγιῶν γενέσθαι τινὰ τρίτην ἄλλην, εἶθ’ ἑξῆς ἁπάσαις ἁπάσας ἐπιπλέκειν, εἶθ’ οὕτω μίαν δυοῖν, εἶτα τρισὶν, εἶτα πλείοσιν ἄχρι περ ἂν ἁπάσας τοῦ συμπλεκομένου τύπου τὰς συζυγίας ἀναμίξῃς τῇ μιᾷ· μετὰ δὲ τοῦτο δύο συζυγίας ἑνὸς τύπου τοῦ πεμπταίου μιᾷ καθ’ ἑκάστην τῶν ἄλλων μιγνύειν, εἶτα δυοῖν, ἢ τριῶν, ἢ τέτταρσιν, ἄχρι περ ἂν ἁπάσας ἀλλήλαις ἐπιπλέξῃς· εἶθ’ οὕτω πάλιν τέτταρας συζυγίας ταῖς καθ’ ἕκαστον τύπον μιγνύειν, εἶτα πέντε, κᾄπειτα ἓξ, μέχρι περ ἂν ἁπάσας τοῦ πεμπταίου τὰς συζυγίας ἁπάσαις τῶν ἄλλων ἀναμίξῃς, οὐχ ὁμοῦ δηλονότι πάντων, ἀλλ’ ἑκάστου κατὰ μόνας, οἷον τὰς τοῦ πεμπταίου ταῖς κατὰ τὸν ἑβδομαῖον, εἶθ’ οὕτω ταῖς κατὰ τὸν ὀγδοαῖον, ἢ τὸν ἐνναταῖον, ἢ τὸν δεκαταῖον, ἤ τινα τῶν ἐφεξῆς· εἶθ’ ὥσπερ τὸν πεμπταῖον ἑκάστῳ τῶν ἄλλων ἔμιξας, οὕτως ἤδη τὸν δεκαταῖον ἑκάστῳ τῶν ἄλλων μιγνύειν, ἔπειθ’ ἑβδομαῖόν τε καὶ ὀγδοαῖον καὶ τοὺς ἄλλους.
english_sentence_A: For each of the types it will first be necessary to go through the variety of the conjunctions, as I showed a little earlier in the case of the quintan; after this, to interweave them with one another, [506] first one conjunction of those from the quintan, let us say, with one of those belonging to the sextan, so that from two conjunctions some other, third one arises; then in sequence to interweave all with all; then in this way one with two, then with three, then with more, until you have mixed all the conjunctions of the type being combined with the one; after this, to mix two conjunctions of one type, the quintan, with one in each of the others, then with two, or three, or four, until you have interwoven them all with one another; then again in this way to mix four conjunctions with those in each type, then five, then six, until you have mixed all the conjunctions of the quintan with all those of the others—not, obviously, of all of them together, but of each one separately, for instance those of the quintan with those of the septan, then in the same way with those of the octan, or the nonan, or the decan, or one of those that follow; then, just as you mixed the quintan with each of the others, so now to mix the decan with each of the others, and then the septan and the octan and the rest.
english_sentence_B: For each of the types it will first be necessary to go through the variety of the combinations, as I showed a little earlier in the case of the quintan; after this, to interweave them with one another, [506] first one combination of those from the quintan, let us say, with one of those of the sextan, so that from two combinations some other, third, comes about; then next to interweave all with all, and so one with two, then with three, then with more, until you have mixed all the combinations of the type being interwoven with the one; after this, to mix two combinations of one type, the quintan, with one of each of the others, then with two, or three, or four, until you have interwoven all with one another; then in this way again to mix four combinations with those of each type, then five, and then six, until you have mixed all the combinations of the quintan with all those of the others: not, obviously, with all of them at once, but with each separately, for example those of the quintan with those of the septan, then in this way with those of the octan, or the nonan, or the decan, or any of those that follow. N. 4.51 , X. HG 6.1.7 , etc.): generally, mainland, opp. islands, Hdt. 1.148 , 171 , al., Th. 1.5 , Philostr. VA 1.20 , etc. later, a continent, esp. of Asia. Hdt. 1.96 , 4.91 , A. Pers. 718 (troch.), X. HG 3.1.5 , D. 60.11 , etc.; ῥεῖθρον ἠπείροιν (-ων codd.) ὅρον, of the Tanais or Phasis, A. Pr. 790 ; so δισσαὶ ἄπειροι, i.e. Europe and Asia, S. Tr. 101 (lyr.); τὼ δύ' ἠπείρω Id. Fr. 881 ; ἐφ' ἑκατέρας τῆς ἠ. Isoc. 4.35 ; ἤ. δοιαί, δίδυμαι, ἀμφότεραι, Mosch. 2.8 , AP 7.18 (Antip. Thess.), 240 (Adaeus), Lib. Ep. 783.3 ; ῥίζαν ἀπείρον τρίταν, of Libya, Pi. P. 9.8 . plain, opp. mountain, ἤπειρόνδε A.R. 2.734 , 976 . in Egypt, land above inundationlevel, PGiss. 48.8 (iii A.D.); more freq., γῆ ἤ. PLond. 3.1201.2 (ii B.C.), etc. (Fr. ἀπερ-yos, cf. Germ. Ufer. )
greek_sentence: ὅτι δ’ οὕτω πολὺ πλῆθος ἔσται τῶν συζυγιῶν, ὡς δυσαριθμήτους γενέσθαι μυριάδας, ἤδη νομίζω κατανοεῖν τινα, κᾂν ἄπειρος ἀριθμοῦ ᾖ.
english_sentence_A: And that the multitude of the conjunctions will be so great that the myriads become hard to count, I think anyone already perceives, even if he be without experience of number.
english_sentence_B: That the multitude of combinations will be so great as to amount to myriads scarcely to be counted, I think anyone already perceives, even if he is inexperienced in number.

lsj_entry_text: ἀριθμ-ητικός, ή, όν, of or for reckoning, skilled therein, ἄνθρωπος Id. Grg. 453e . arithmetical, μέσα Archyt. 2 ; ἀναλογία Arist. EN 1106a35 ; τὸ ἓν ἁπλῶς οὐκ ἦν ἀ. Dam. Pr. 117 ; ἡ ἀριθμητική (sc. τέχνη) arithmetic, Pl. R. 525a , al.; as a subject of competition, Inscr.Magn. 107 ; ἡ ἀ. ἐπιστήμη Plu. 2.979e . Adv. -κῶς ib. 643c , Theo Sm. p.116H. -κόν, τό, land-tax in Egypt, τὸ τέλειον ἀ. Sammelb. 4415.14 (ii A. D.), etc.; ἡμιτέλειον ἀ. BGU 330.6 (ii A. D.).
greek_sentence: δύναται δὲ καὶ τοῖς ἀριθμητικοῖς κοινωσάμενος τὸν λόγον, ἀκοῦσαι παρ’ αὐτῶν τὸ πλῆθος.
english_sentence_A: He can also, by communicating the matter to the arithmeticians, hear from them the total.
english_sentence_B: He can also share the reasoning with the arithmeticians and hear the multitude from them.

lsj_entry_text: χρήσιμ-ος, η, ον, also ος, ον X. Mem. 3.8.8 , Pl. Grg. 480b , R. 333b : (χράμαι):— useful, serviceable, first in Thgn. 406 ; εἰς ἀνάγκαν, ἔνθ' οὐ ποδὶ χρησίμῳ χρῆται S. OT 878 (lyr.); τὸ χ. φρενῶν the excellence of . . , E. Ph. 1740 (lyr.); τὸ αὐτίκα χ. Th. 3.56 ; ἡ διὰ τὸ χ. φιλία Arist. EN 1159b13 ; τὰ χ. Men. Mon. 579 ; χ. εἴς τι useful for something, Hdt. 4.109 , Ar. Pl. 493 (anap.), Pl. R. l. c.; ἐπί τι Id.Grg. l. c.; πρός τι E. Hipp. 482 ( Comp. ); ἰδίᾳ ἑκάστῳ χ. καὶ ὑπὲρ τοῦ κοινοῦ ὠφέλιμα X. Cyr. 6.2.34 ; τοῦτ' οὖν τί ἐστι χρήσιμον; Ar. Nu. 202 ; χρήσιμόν ἐστι, c. inf., Id. Av. 382 (troch.). of persons, serviceable, useful, S. Aj. 410 , D. 20.7 , etc.; Comp. -ώτερος Pl. Lg. 819c : esp., like χρηστός , a good and useful citizen, χ. πόλει E. Or. 910 ; χ. πολίτης Eup. 118 ; χ. τινι Is. Fr. 16.1 ; ἐπί τι D. 25.31 ; τοὺς εὐπόρους δεῖ χ. αὑτοὺς παρέχειν τοῖς πολίταις to show themselves useful, serviceable to the state, Id. 42.22 , cf. E. Supp. 887 , Is. Fr. 10.1 ( Comp. ); τοῖς σώμασι -ώτεροι more able-bodied, X. Lac. 5.9 ; opp. ἀργαλέος τὴν ὄψιν, Aeschin. 1.61 . used, made use of, τέμενος -ώτατον a muchfrequented sanctuary, dub. in Hdt. 2.178 . χρησίμη διαθήκη an available (i.e. authentic) will, Is. 6.30 . νομίσματα οὐ χρήσιμα ἔξω money that will not pass abroad, X. Vect. 3.2 . Adv., -μως ἔχειν to be serviceable, Th. 3.44 , X. Cyr. 8.5.9 ; χ. τινὶ σωθῆναι with advantage to him, Th. 5.91 , cf. J. BJ 6.2.9 ; τὰ -μως λεγόμενα Plu. 2.36d .
greek_sentence: εἰ μὲν οὖν χρήσιμον εἶναι νομίζουσιν ἐπιπλέκειν ἀλλήλοις τύπους, ἴστωσαν τοῦ χρησίμου τὸ μυριοστὸν μέρος εὑρηκότες· εἰ δ’ ἄχρηστον, αἰδεσθέντες ἤδη ποτὲ καλέσωσιν, ἐπὶ τὰς βίβλους τὸν Ἥφαιστον, ἢ κᾂν αὐτοὶ μὴ καλέσωσιν, ὁ χρόνος αὐτὰς διαφθερεῖ.
english_sentence_A: If, then, they think it useful to intertwine types with one another, let them know that they have discovered the ten-thousandth part of what is useful; but if useless, let them, being ashamed, at last some day summon Hephaestus upon their books; or, even if they themselves do not summon him, time will destroy them.
english_sentence_B: If, then, they think it useful to interweave types with one another, let them know that they have found the ten-thousandth part of what is useful; but if it is useless, let them now at last, out of shame, summon Hephaestus to their books; or even if they themselves do not summon him, time will destroy them.

lsj_entry_text: ἐφήμερ-ος, ον, Dor. ἐπάμ- Pi. P. 8.95 , Fr. 182 (ἐφαμ- I. 7(6).40 , Fr. 157 ): (ἡμέρα):—more common form of ἐφημέριος, esp. in Prose, living but a day: hence, short-lived, τερπνόν id.I.l.c.; τύχαι E. Heracl. 866 , Diph. 45 ; ὄλβος οὐ βέβαιος, ἀλλ' ἐ. E. Ph. [558] ; ἐ. σώματα καὶ χρήματα ἡγεῖσθαι Th. 2.53 ; χρῆσις Arist. Pol. 1252b16 ; ἐ. καὶ προπετῆ βίον Men. 382 ; τὸ ἐ. Arist. EN 1096b5 ; ἐ. πᾶν τὸ τῶν πολλῶν ἀγαθόν Epicur. Fr. 489 . of men, ἐφήμεροι creatures of a day, Pi. P. 8.95 , Semon. 1.3 , A. Pr. 83 ; ὦ τάλας ἐφάμερε Pi. Fr. 157 ; ὦφήμερε Ar. Nu. 223 ; ὦ φίλοι καὶ ἀτεχνῶς ἐ. Pl. Lg. 923a . for the day, daily, πυρετός Hp. Aph. 4.55 ; τροφή D.H. 8.41 , Ep.Jac. 2.15 , Vett.Val. 62.17 . cf. D.S. 3.32 (pl.); γυμνασία Ascl. Tact. 1.4 ; πράξεις Luc. Pseudol. 17 ; δαπάνη Plu. Per. 16 , etc.: neut. pl. as Adv., once a day, Orib. Eup. 1.9 . φάρμακον ἐ. killing on the same day, Plu. Them. 31 .
greek_sentence: τίς δὲ οὐ καὶ ταύταις ἤδη κατατεμὼν εἰς τὰς ἐφημέρους χρείας ἀναλώσει;
english_sentence_A: And who will not already cut up even these and use them up for everyday needs?
english_sentence_B: And who will not cut these too into pieces and use them up for his everyday needs?

lsj_entry_text: διάγραμμα, ατος, τό, figure marked out by lines, plan, Pl. R. 529e : esp. geometrical figure, X. Mem. 4.7.3 , Pl. Phd. 73b , Arist. Cael. 280a1 , etc. geometrical proposition, Id. EN 1112b21 , APr. 41b14 , Ascl. in Metaph. 174.9 . in Music, scale, Phan.Hist. 17 ; but ἀφ' ἑνὸς δ. ὑποκρέκειν on one note, Plu. 2.55d , cf. Dem. 13 . horoscope, nativity, Id. Mar. 42 . map, Jul. Ep. 10 . list, register, D. 14.21 ; inventory, σκευῶν Id. 47.36 ; register of taxable property, PRev.Laws 39.17 , al. (iii B. C.), Harp. , Suid. ordinance, regulation, GDI 5040.64 (Cret.), PEleph. 14.27 (iii B. C.), D.S. 18.57 ; τὸ δ. τῶ Ἀντιγόνω OGI 7 (Cyme); = Lat. edictum, Plb. 22.10.6 , Plu. Marc. 24 .
greek_sentence: Τούτων ἤδη γεγραμμένων, καί τισι τῶν ἑταίρων ἐκδιδομένων, ἢ ἀξιωσάντων ἑτέρων μαθεῖν, ὅπως ἂν ᾖ τοῦ [508] διαγράμματος, ἐγὼ παραχρῆμα τοῖς προβάλλουσιν ἀποκρίνομαι τὸ πλῆθος τῶν τύπων.
english_sentence_A: These things having already been written and given out to some of my companions, or when others asked to learn how it might be done apart from the [508] diagram, I straightway answer those who put the question with the number of the types.
english_sentence_B: When this had already been written and was being handed out to some of my companions, or rather when others asked to learn how it might be [done] with regard to the [508] diagram, I give those who pose the problem the number of the types on the spot.

lsj_entry_text: πρότερος and πρῶτος, Comp. and Sup. formed from πρό, opp. ὕστερος, ὕστατος. Comp. πρότερος, α, ον, of Place, before, in front, π. πόδες the fore-feet, Od. 19.228 ; π. ἵπποι horses in front, B. 5.43 :— but mostly, of Time, former, earlier, ἄνδρες Il. 21.405 ; ἄνθρωποι 5.637 , 23.332 ; οἱ π. men of former times, 4.308 (rarely without Art., A. Ag. 1338 (anap.), etc.); οὗτος δὲ προτέρης γενεῆς π. τ' ἀνθρώπων Il. 23.790 : also, older, opp. ὁπλότερος, 2.707 , etc.; γενεῇ π. 15.182 ; but παῖδες π. children by the first or a former marriage, Od. 15.22 ; παῖδες ἐκ τῆς π. γυναικός Hdt. 7.2 ; τῇ προτέρῃ (sc. ἡμέρᾳ) on the day before, Od. 16.50 ; ἠοῖ τῇ π. Il. 13.794 (in Prose more freq. τῇ προτεραίᾳ, cf. προτεραῖος); τοῦ π. ἐνιαυτοῦ the year before, IG 12.352.11 ; τοῖς π. Παναθηναίοις the preceding P., ib. 57.8 ; τὰ π. what has preceded, Plot. 3.2.8 :—freq. used predicatively, sts. where we should expect the Adv. (which is never used by Hom. ), ὅ με π. κάκ' ἔοργε Il. 3.351 , cf. 16.569 , Hes. Op. 708 , etc.; σπονδὰς οὐ λύσετε πρότεροι Th. 1.123 ; οἱ π. ἐπιόντες ibid.; τοῖς π. μετὰ Κύρου ἀναβᾶσι X. An. 1.4.12 , cf. IG 22.1.7 ; εἰ μὴ π. ἑωράκη αὐτὸν ἢ ἐκεῖνος ἐμέ Pl. R. 336d , cf. 432c , etc.; ὅτι εἴη π. ὑπὸ ἐκείνων ἠδικημένος PCair.Zēn. 288.9 (iii B.C.). as regular Comp. , c. gen., ἐμέο πρότερος Il. 10.124 ; π. τούτων Hdt. 1.168 , cf. Pl. Phd. 86b , Hp.Ma. 282d ; τὰς γυναῖκας μὴ ἀπιέναι προτέρας τῶν ἀνδρῶν IG 12(5).593.19 (Iulis, v B.C.); τῇ π. ἡμέρᾳ τῆς τροπῆς the day before . . , Arist. Pol. 1316a16 ; προτέρᾳ εἰδυῶν Ὀκτωμβρίων IG 7.2225.14 (Thisbe, Senatus Consultum, ii B.C.); τῷ π. ἔτει Παναθηναίων τῶν μεγάλων ib. 22.212.27 ; τῷ π. ἔτει τῆς ἥττης Plb. 2.43.6 : folld. by ἤ, τῷ προτέρῳ ἔτεϊ ἢ τὸν κρητῆρα [ἐληΐσαντο] Hdt. 3.47 . of Rank, Worth, and generally of Precedence, superior, τῷ γένει, τῇ δυνάμει, Is. 1.17 , D. 3.15 ; π. τινὸς πρός τι superior to him in . . , Pl. La. 183b ; π. τι ἄγειν, π. ποιήσασθαι τὰ σὰ πράγματα, Lib. Or. 58.36 , 52.1 . after Hom. , neut. πρότερον freq. as Adv., before, earlier, Pi. O. 13.31 , Hdt. 4.45 , IG 12.374.265 , etc.; ὀλίγον π. Pl. Prt. 317e : c. gen., π. φήμης A. Th. 866 (anap.); ὀλίγῳ τι π. τούτων Hdt. 8.95 ; πολλοῖσι ἔτεσι π. τούτων ib. 96 ; ἐνιαυτῷ π. τῆς ἁλώσεως D. 9.60 ; also πρὸ τῶν Περσικῶν δέκα ἔτεσι π. Pl. Lg. 642d , cf. Criti. 112a ; τούτου π. Paus. 1.1.2 : most freq. folld. by ἤ, π. ἢ κατὰ τὴν προσδοκίαν Pl. Sph. 264b ; also μὴ π. ἀπαναστῆναι ἢ ἐξέλωσι Hdt. 9.87 , cf. 7.54 , Antipho 2.1.2 , Th. 7.63 , etc.: with inf., π. ἢ βασιλεῦσαι Hdt. 7.2 , cf. Th. 1.69 , etc.: folld. by πρίν, Hdt. 1.82 ; by πρὶν ἄν, ib. 140 ; by πρὶν ἤ with vb. in Indic., Id. 6.45 , 8.8 , or Subj., 7.8 .β ́ ( v.l. πρὶν ἂν ἢ ), 9.93 ; also οὐ π. εἰ μὴ . . Plu. Lys. 10 , etc.; οὐ π. ἕως . . , or ἕως ἂν . . , Lys. 12.71 , Ath. 14.640c ; μὴ π., ἀλλ' ὅταν . . Plb. 9.13.3 : also used with the Art., τὸ π. Pl. R. 522a , X. An. 4.4.14 , etc. (τὸ π., also, for the first time, Ep. Gal. 4.13 ): c. gen., τὸ π. τῶν ἀνδρῶν τούτων Hdt. 2.144 : the Adv. is freq. put between Art. and Subst., ὁ π. βασιλεύς Id. 1.84 ; τὰ π. ἀδικήματα Id. 6.87 ; αἱ π. ἁμαρτίαι Ar. Eq. 1355 , etc. Sup. πρῶτος, η, ον, Dor. πρᾶτος (q.v.): as Adj., of Place, foremost, πρώτοισιν ἐνὶ προμάχοισι μιγέντα Od. 18.379 ; ἐν πρώτοις, μετὰ πρώτοισι alone, Il. 19.424 , 11.64 ; πρώτῃ ἐν ὑσμίνῃ, ἐνὶ πρώτῳ ὁμάδῳ, 15.340 , 17.380 ; τῆς πρώτης τάττειν (sc. τάξεως) Isoc. 12.180 , cf. Lys. 16.15 , etc.; ἐν π. ῥυμῷ at the front or end of the pole, Il. 6.40 , 16.371 ; πρώτῃσι θύρῃσιν at the outermost doors, 22.66 ; π. ξύλον the front bench, Ar. Ach. 25 , Poll. 4.121 , etc.; οἱ π. πόδες, like πρόσθιοι , Id. 1.193 . of Time, στάντα πρὸς π. ἕω looking towards first dawn, S. OC 477 ; περὶ π. νύκτα Poll. 1.70 . of Order, serving as ordinal to εἷς, ἄεθλα θῆκε . . τῷ πρώτῳ· ἀτὰρ αὖ τῷ δευτέρῳ . . , αὐτὰρ τῷ τριτάτῳ . . , κτλ., Il. 23.265 , cf. 6.179 ; opp. ὕστατος, 2.281 , 5.703 , etc.; opp. τελευταῖος, A. Ag. 314 ; opp. τανύστατος, Od. 9.449 ; πρῶτοι πάντων ἀνθρώπων Hdt. 2.2 ; τὰ π. τῶν ὀνομάτων Pl. Cra. 421d ; τῇ π. τῶν ἡμερέων Hdt. 7.168 , etc.; π. ἄξων IG 12.115.10 ; ἐπὶ τοῦ π. [ἱερείου] first-offered, X. An. 4.3.9 ; ἐν τοῖς π. λόγοις in the earlier books, Arist. Ph. 263a11 , al.; ἐν πρώτοις among the first, Is. 7.40 ; hence, above all, especially, Hdt. 8.69 , Pl. R. 522c ; in Att. , ἐν τοῖς πρῶτοι (v. ὁ, ἡ , τό A. VIII. 6 ):—freq. used predicatively of being the first to do something, Νέστωρ πρῶτος κτύπον ἄϊε Il. 10.532 ; πρῶτος ἀνατέλλει Eratosth. Cal. 42 ; εἴθε π. σοι ἐνέτυχον Luc. Tyr. 21 . Philos., first in order of existence, primary, αἱ π. οὐσίαι Arist. Cat. 2b26 , cf. Metaph. 1032b2 ; π. ὕλη, π. φιλοσοφία, ib. 1015a7 , 1061b19 ; primitive, simple, οἰκία π., ἡ π. πόλις, Id. Pol. 1252b10 , 1291a17 ; ἡ π. κοινωνία ib. 1257a19 ; ἡ π. ὀλιγαρχία ib. 1293a14 ; ὁ π. συλλογισμός normal, typical, Id. Rh. 1357a17 ; τὰ π. σώματα, μόρια,= τὰ ὁμοιομερῆ, Gal. 5.673 , 674 ; πρῶτα κατὰ φύσιν, e.g. health, perception, Stoic. 3.34 ; τὰ π. πάθη ib. 92 ; αἱ π. ἀρεταί ib. 64 . Math., πρῶτοι ἀριθμοί prime numbers, Euc. 7 Def. 11 , 12 ; but also, first numbers (= 1 to 100 , 000 , 000 ) in the notation of Archim., Aren. 3.2 . πρῶτος is sts. used where we should expect πρότερος, Αἰνείας δὲ πρῶτος ἀκόντισεν Il. 13.502 , cf. 18.92 : in late Greek folld. by gen., πρῶτός μου ἦν Ev.Jo. 1.15 , 30 , cf. 15.18 ; οἱ πρῶτοί μου ταῦτα ἀνιχνεύσαντες Ael. NA 8.12 ; πρώτη εὕρηται ἡ περὶ τοὺς πόδας κίνησις τῆς διὰ τῶν χειρῶν Ath. 14.630c ; γεννήτορα πρῶτον μητέρος εἰς ἀΐδην πέμψει Man. 1.329 , 4.404 ; ἀλόχου πρῶτος before his wife, IG 12(5).590.5 (vi (?) A.D. ). of Rank or Dignity, μετὰ πρώτοισιν among the first men of the state, Od. 6.60 , etc.; νομίσαντες πρῶτοι ἂν εἶναι Th. 6.28 ; διαβάλλειν τοὺς π. X. An. 2.6.26 , cf. Arist. Pol. 1266a18 ; αἱ π. πόλεις Th. 2.8 ; ὁ π. ἄρχων IG 12(3).481.10 (Thera), CIG 2837 (Aphrodisias); ὁ π. τῆς πόλεως, as a title, IG 12(5).292.2 (Paros); ὁ π. τῆς νήσου Act.Ap. 28.7 ; τῶν π. φίλων, title at the Ptolemaic court, PTeb. 31.15 (ii B.C.), etc.; τῶν π., as military title, PHib. 1.110.72 (iii B.C.), PPetr. 3p.23 (iii B.C.), PTeb. 815 Fr. 4.23 ,al.(iii B.C.): c. gen., ἐν πρώτοισι Μυκηναίων Il. 15.643 ; οἱ π. στρατοῦ S. Ph. 1305 , cf. E. Hec. 304 , etc.: c. dat. modi, ἀρετῇ π., οἱ π. καὶ χρήμασι καὶ γένει, πλούτῳ π. τῶν Ἑλλήνων, etc., S. Ph. 1425 , Th. 3.65 , Isoc. 16.31 , etc.; π. ἐν συμφοραῖς βίου S. OT 33 . of Degree, first, highest, μοῖρα Id. OC 145 (anap.), etc. as Subst. in neut. pl. πρῶτα, τά , (sc. ἆθλα), first prize, τὰ π. λαβών Il. 23.275 ; τὰ π. δόρει κρατύνων S. OC 1313 ; ἔχειν πρῶτα κυναγεσίας AP 6.118 (Antip.); τὰ π. φέρεσθαι D.C. 42.57 , etc. first part, beginning, τῆς Ἰλιάδος τὰ π. Pl. R. 392e ; ἐν τοῖς π. Id. Smp. 221d ; τὸ π. τοῦ ᾄσματος Id. Prt. 343c . first, highest, in degree, τὰ π. τᾶς λιμῶ ( Dor. ) the extremities of famine, Ar. Ach. 743 (nisi leg. ἄπρατα) ; ἐχέτωσαν τὰ π. τῆς εὐδαιμονίας Luc. Cont. 10 ; ἐς τὰ π. τιμᾶσθαι Th. 3.39 , cf. 56 ; φρενῶν ἐς τὰ ἐμεωυτοῦ π. οὔκω ἀνήκω I have not yet come to the highest development of my judgment, Hdt. 7.13 , cf. D.C. 38.22 ; of persons, ἐὼν τῶν Ἐρετριέων τὰ π. Hdt. 6.100 ; Λάμπων . . Αἰγινητέων <ἐὼν> τὰ π. Id. 9.78 , cf. E. Med. 917 ; ἐστὶν τὰ π. τῆς ἐκεῖ μοχθηρίας (of a person) Ar. Ra. 421 . Philos., primary things, elements, Emp. 38.1 , Arist. GC 335a29 ; τὰ π. αἴτια Id. Mete. 338a20 ; also τὸ π. ἐνυπάρχον ἑκάστῳ Id. Ph. 193a10 . in Logic, the first undemonstrable propositions, on which all future conclusions rest, Id. Top. 100b18 ; τὰ π. ἀναπόδεικτα Id. APo. 71b26 . in Adverbial phrases, τὴν πρώτην (sc. ὥραν, ὁδόν) first, for the present, just now, Hdt. 3.134 , Ar. Th. 662 , D. 3.2 , Arist. Metaph. 1038a35 , etc.; τὴν πρώτην εἶναι Hdt. 1.153 . with Preps., ἀπὸ πρώτης (sc. ἀρχῆς) Antipho 5.56 , Th. 1.77 ; ἀπὸ τῆς π. εὐθύς Luc. Hist.Conscr. 1 ; ἐκ π. Babr. 45.14 ; κατὰ πρώτας Pl. english_sentence_A: You too will be persuaded that this is so, if you first recall, and always keep ready to hand the memory of, these points: that in this account we call a 'day' the time composed of the day and the night, which some name a nychthemeron.
english_sentence_B: You yourself will also be persuaded that this is so if you first recall, and always keep readily at hand the memory of these things, that in this [reckoning of] time we call 'day' the time composed of both the day and the night, which some call the nychthemeron. Thus, indeed, we also say that the year is of 365 days and a quarter.

english_sentence_A: Of one day, then, there are twenty-four hours, of two forty-eight, of three seventy-two; but the names of the types are derived not from the days completed, but from the return of the paroxysm.
english_sentence_B: But the names of the types are taken not from the days that are completed, but from the return of the paroxysm. We call tertian that in which the paroxysm occurs every third day, two [days] evidently being completed in between.

greek_sentence: τριταῖον μὲν ὀνομάζομεν ᾧ διὰ τρίτης ἡμέρας ὁ παροξυσμὸς γίγνεται, δυοῖν μεταξὺ δηλονότι καὶ συμπληρωθεισῶν· τεταρταῖον δὲ ᾧ κατὰ τετάρτην, τριῶν κᾀπὶ τούτῳ μεταξὺ συμπληρουμένων ἡμερῶν, ἐπί τε τῶν ἄλλων ἀνάλογον· ὥσθ’ ὅταν εὕρῃς περίοδον τύπου τεττάρων ἡμερῶν, πεμπταῖον ἐρεῖς αὐτὸν, οὐ ταὐτὸν γάρ ἐστι διὰ πέμπτης τε παροξύνεσθαι καὶ πέντε ἡμερῶν ἔχειν περίοδον.
english_sentence_A: We call tertian that in which the paroxysm occurs on every third day, two days, evidently, being completed in between; quartan that in which it occurs on the fourth, three days in this case too being completed in between; and analogously in the other cases; so that when you find a period of a type of four days, you will call it quintan, for it is not the same thing to suffer the paroxysm on every fifth day and to have a period of five days.
english_sentence_B: We call quartan that in which it occurs on the fourth, three days in this case too being completed in between, and in the other cases proportionally. So when you find a period of a type of four days, you will call it quintan; for to have paroxysms every fifth day is not the same as to have a period of five days.

Ep. 326e (and Pass. , ἀρχαὶ βέβληνται Pi. N. 1.8 ); ἀρχὴν ἄρχεσθαί τινος Pl. Ti. 36e ; source of action, [ ὁ ἄνθρωποσ] ἔχει ἀρχὴν ἐλευθέραν Plot. 3.3.4 . with Preps. in adverbial usages, ἐξ ἀρχῆς from the beginning, from the first, from of old, Od. 1.188 , Xenoph. 10 , etc.; οὑξ ἀ. φίλος S. OT 385 ; ἡ ἐξ ἀ. ἔχθρα D. 54.3 ; τὸ ἐξ ἀ. X. Cyn. 12.6 ; but πλουτεῖν ἐξ ἀ. πάλιν anew, afresh, Ar. Pl. 221 ; λόγον πάλιν ὥσπερ ἐξ ἀ. κινεῖν Pl. R. 450a ; ὁ ἐξ ἀ. λόγος the original argument, Id. Tht. 177c , etc.; τὰ ἐξ ἀ. the principal sum, Arist. Pol. 1280a30 :—also ἀπ' ἀ. Hes. Th. 425 , Hdt. 2.104 , Pi. P. 8.25 , A. Supp. 344 , Pl. Tht. 206d ; κατ' ἀρχάς in the beginning, at first, Hdt. 3.153 , 7.5 ; αὐτίκα κατ' ἀ. Id. 8.94 ; τὸ κατ' ἀ. Pl. Lg. 798a , al. acc. ἀρχήν, abs., to begin with, at first, Hdt. 1.9 , 2.28 , 8.132 ; τὴν ἀρχήν And. 3.20 : pl., τὰς ἀρχάς Plb. 16.22.8 : freq. followed by a neg., not at all, ἀρχὴν μηδὲ λαβών Hdt. 3.39 , cf. 1.193 , al.; ἀ. δὲ θηρᾶν οὐ πρέπει τἀμήχανα S. Ant. 92 ; ἀ. κλύειν ἂν οὐκ . . ἐβουλόμην Id. Ph. 1239 , cf. El. 439 , Philol. 3 , Antipho 5.73 , Pl. Grg. 478c ; sts. c. Art., τοῦτο οὐκ ἐνδέκομαι τὴν ἀ. Hdt. 4.25 ; τὴν ἀ. γὰρ ἐξῆν αὐτῷ μὴ γράφειν D. 23.93 . first principle, element, first so used by Anaximander, acc. to Simp. in Ph. 150.23 , cf. Arist. Metaph. 983b11 , etc.; Ἡράκλειτος τὴν ἀ. εἶναί φησι ψυχήν Id. de An. 405a25 ; of ὕλη and θεός, opp. στοιχεῖα, Placit. 1.3.25 ; practical principle of conduct, τῶν πράξεων τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ὑποθέσεις D. 2.10 ; principles of knowledge, Arist. Metaph. 995b8 , al. end, corner, of a bandage, rope, sheet, etc., Hdt. 4.60 , Hp. Off. 9 , E. Hipp. 762 , Aen.Tact. 18.14 , Act.Ap. 10.11 ; of a compound pulley, Hero Bel. 84.14 . Math., origin of a curve, τῆς ἕλικος Archim. Spir. 11 Def. 2 , etc.; ξυνὸν ἀ. καὶ πέρας ἐπὶ κύκλου περιφερείας Heraclit. 103 . branch of a river, LXX Ge. 2.10 (pl.). sum, total, ib. Nu. 1.2 . vital organs of the body, Gal. 1.318 , al. first place or power, sovereignty (not in Hom. ), Διὸς ἀρχά Pi. O. 2.64 , cf. Hdt. 1.6 , etc.; γενέσθαι ἐπ' ἀρχῆς Arist. Pol. 1284b2 : metaph., μεγάλην μεντἂν ἀ. εἴης εὑρηκώς, of a stroke of fortune, D. 21.196 : pl., ἀρχαὶ πολισσονόμοι A. Ch. 864 (lyr.); τὰς ἐμὰς ἀρχὰς σέβων S. Ant. 744 , etc.: c. gen. rei, τῆσδ' ἔχων ἀρχὴν χθονός S. OT 737 ; ἀ. τῶν νεῶν, τῆς θαλάσσης, power over them, Th. 3.90 , X. Ath. 2.7 , etc.: prov., ἀ. ἄνδρα δείξει Biasap. Arist. EN 1130a1 , cf. D. Prooem. 48 ; method of government, οὐδὲ τὴν ἄλλην ἀ. ἐπαχθής Th. 6.54 . empire, realm, Κύρου, Περδίκκου ἀ., Hdt. 1.91 , Th. 4.128 , etc. magistracy, office, ἀρχὴν ἄρχειν, παραλαμβάνειν, Hdt. 3.80 , 4.147 ; καταστήσας τὰς ἀ. καὶ ἄρχοντας ἐπιστήσας Id. 3.89 ; εἰς ἀ. καθ<*>στασθαι Th. 8.70 ; εἰς τὴν α<*>. εἰσιέναι D. 59.72 , etc.; ἀ. λαχεῖν to obtain an office, Id. 57.25 ; Ἑλληνοταμίαι τότε πρῶτον κατέστη ἀ. Th. 1.96 ; ἐνιαύσιος ἀ. Id. 6.54 ; ἀ. χειροτονητή, κληρωτή, Lex ap. Aeschin. 1.21 ; withsg. Noun, Κυθηροδίκης ἀ. ἐκ τῆς Σπάρτης διέβαινεν αὐτόσε Th. 4.53 ; term of office, ἀρχῆς λοιποὶ αὐτῷ δύο μῆνες Antipho 6.42 ; ἀρχαὶ καὶ λειτουργίαι POxy. 119.16 (iii A.D.). in pl., αἱ ἀρχαί the authorities, the magistrates, Th. 5.47 , cf. Decr. ap. And. 1.83 ; ἐν ταῖς ἀ. ε<*>ναι Th. 6.54 ; ἡ ἀρχή collectively, 'the board', D. 47.22 , cf. IG 1.229 , etc.; παραδιδόναι τινὰ τῇ ἀ. Antipho 5.48 ; but ἡ ἀ., of a single magistrate, PHal. 1.226 (iii B.C.); κατ' ἀρχῆς γὰρ φιλαίτιος λεώς against authority, A. Supp. 485 ; πομποὺς ἀρχάς Id. Ag. 124 (anap.). command, i.e. body of troops, LXX 1 Ki. 13.17 , al. pl., heavenly powers, Ep.Rom. 8.38 , al., cf. Dam. Pr. 96 ; powers of evil, Ep.Eph. 6.12 , al. = εἶδος μελίσσης ἀκέντρου , Hsch.
greek_sentence: λέλεκται δὲ ὅτι τὸν προβληθέντα περιοδικῶν ἀριθμὸν ὡρῶν, ὃς ἐν τῷ μεταξὺ δυοῖν ἀρχῶν γίνεται παροξυσμὸς, ἐπισκέπτου πότερον μετρεῖ τὸν ἐν τῷ διαγράμματι περιεχόμενον ἀριθμὸν ὁντιναοῦν.
english_sentence_A: It was said that, as to the proposed number of periodic hours — the number which comes to be in the interval between two beginnings of paroxysm — you should examine whether it measures any one whatever of the numbers contained in the diagram.
